stored_procedure_dynamic_csharp.risk: The text of an EXEC or sp_executesql command (which runs a stored procedure, a query saved in the database) is built by joining values with +. If one of them comes from a user, that user can add their own SQL and run any command on the database.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Put a placeholder in the command and pass the value separately: "EXEC GetUser @userName" with cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@userName", userName), or call the procedure with CommandType.StoredProcedure.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

stored_procedure_dynamic_csharp.benefit: A value from a user can no longer change your database commands.

taint_codeinj.title: Code injection: an attacker can make your application run their code
taint_codeinj.risk: Data sent by a visitor is run as code by your application. An attacker can then take control of the server and reach all its data.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Never run data received from a visitor as code: to read a simple value, use ast.literal_eval() instead of eval(), otherwise choose among a fixed list of allowed actions.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_codeinj.benefit: No one can make your application run their own code.

taint_cookie_injection.title: Cookie injection
taint_cookie_injection.risk: An attacker can inject CRLF sequences to set arbitrary cookies, override existing cookies, or split HTTP responses to perform cache poisoning or XSS.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove the line breaks (\r and \n) from the value before putting it in the cookie, or better, accept only the characters you expect.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_cookie_injection.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_deserialization.title: Data from outside is turned back into program objects
taint_deserialization.risk: Some formats rebuild program objects from the bytes received, and can run code while doing so. An attacker who sends crafted data runs their own commands on your server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Read received data with a format that only holds data, such as JSON, or with the safe loading function of your library, never with one that can rebuild any kind of object.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_deserialization.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_graphql_injection.title: A value from the request is pasted into a GraphQL query
taint_graphql_injection.risk: The GraphQL query (the language the API uses to ask for data) is built by pasting in a value sent by the visitor. An attacker can add their own fields or conditions to read data they should not see, or send a query heavy enough to block the server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Pass the value as a variable of the query instead of pasting it in, and limit the depth and complexity of accepted queries.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_graphql_injection.benefit: The visitor can only fill in a value, not change the query.

taint_header_injection.title: A value from the request can add fake headers to the response
taint_header_injection.risk: A value sent by the visitor is copied into a header of the response (the hidden lines sent before the page). If it contains line breaks, an attacker can add their own headers or even a fake page, for example to steal a session.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove the line breaks (\r and \n) from the value before putting it in a header, or reject the request when it contains any.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_header_injection.benefit: The response only carries the headers your code writes.

taint_ldap.title: User data can change a directory (LDAP) search
taint_ldap.risk: A value from the user is placed as it is in an LDAP search (the directory of users and groups). By adding characters such as * or ), an attacker can change the search, for example to log in without a password or list every account.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Escape the value (neutralize its special characters) before putting it in the search, with the escape function of your LDAP library.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_ldap.benefit: The user can only fill in a value, not change the search itself.

taint_log_injection.title: A value from the request can add fake lines to the log
taint_log_injection.risk: A value sent by the visitor reaches the log as it is. If it contains line breaks, an attacker can add fake lines to the log, for example to hide an attack or mislead whoever reads it.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove the line breaks and control characters (\r, \n) from the value before writing it to the log, then pass it as a parameter of the log call.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_log_injection.benefit: Each line of the log matches a real event.

taint_nosql.title: NoSQL injection
taint_nosql.risk: An attacker can inject MongoDB query operators (e.g., $where, $gt) to bypass authentication, extract data from unauthorized collections, or cause denial of service.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Check that the value is a plain text or number before the query, and accept only the characters you expect, so that it can never be read as a search condition.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_nosql.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_open_redirect.title: Open redirect: a link to your site can lead visitors to a fake site
taint_open_redirect.risk: Your site redirects the visitor to an address taken from the request, such as ?next=. An attacker can send a link that starts with your real address but leads to a fake site, for example to steal passwords.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Only redirect to pages of your own site: check that the requested address is a path of your site (it starts with / but not with //) and use "/" otherwise.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_open_redirect.benefit: Links to your site can no longer be used to send visitors elsewhere.

taint_path_traversal.title: Access to files outside the intended folder
taint_path_traversal.risk: A file name sent by a visitor is used to open a file on the server. With « ../ » an attacker can read or write other files, such as your passwords or your configuration.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Check the path before opening the file: 1) compute the full path with os.path.realpath(); 2) reject it if it does not start with the allowed folder.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_path_traversal.benefit: A visitor can only open the files you planned for.

taint_rce.title: Command injection: an attacker can run commands on the server
taint_rce.risk: Data sent by a visitor is placed in a system command run by your application. An attacker can then run their own commands on the server and take control of it.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Do not build the command as text: call subprocess.run() with a list [program, argument] and shell=False, and accept only values planned in advance.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_rce.benefit: No one can run their own commands on your server.

taint_smtp_injection.title: SMTP injection
taint_smtp_injection.risk: An attacker can inject additional email headers (Cc, Bcc, Subject) to send spam, relay malicious emails, or exfiltrate data via the email server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove the line breaks (\r and \n) from every value that goes into an email header, and check each address with an email validation function before using it.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_smtp_injection.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_sqli.title: SQL injection: an attacker can read or change your database
taint_sqli.risk: Data sent by a visitor is inserted as it is into a database query. An attacker can then read, change or delete your data, including that of other users.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Pass the data to the query as a parameter instead of inserting it into its text: write the query with a placeholder (? or %s depending on your library) and give the value separately.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_sqli.benefit: Your data can no longer be read or changed through a crafted query.

taint_ssrf.title: Taint SSRF
taint_ssrf.risk: An attacker can make the server send requests to internal services.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Accept only the hosts you expect: parse the address and call it only if its host is in your list of allowed hosts.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_ssrf.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_ssti.title: Taint SSTI
taint_ssti.risk: An attacker can execute arbitrary code on the server via template injection, often leading to full Remote Code Execution.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Keep templates in files you wrote, and pass the visitor's data to them as values instead of building a template from that data.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_ssti.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_xpathi.title: Taint XPath Injection
taint_xpathi.risk: An attacker can manipulate XPath queries to bypass authentication, enumerate XML nodes, or extract sensitive data from XML documents.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Pass the value as a variable of the XPath query instead of pasting it into the query text; when your library has no XPath variables, accept only the characters you expect, such as letters and digits.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_xpathi.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_xss.title: Malicious code injected into your pages (XSS)
taint_xss.risk: Data sent by a visitor is shown as it is in a web page. An attacker can slip in a script that runs for other users and steals their session or their credentials.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Let your template engine escape the data (Jinja2 or Django, without |safe or Markup()), or use html.escape(): its special characters are then no longer read as code.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_xss.benefit: Your pages no longer run code supplied by a visitor.

taint_xxe.title: Taint XXE
taint_xxe.risk: An attacker can read local files, perform SSRF, or cause denial of service via malicious XML containing external entity references.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Turn off external entities (references to other files or addresses) in the XML parser before reading data from outside, or use a parser that blocks them by default.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_xxe.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

unbounded_allocation_from_input.title: The size of a memory buffer is taken from the request without a limit
unbounded_allocation_from_input.risk: The program reserves memory with a size that comes from the request, such as the Content-Length header (the size announced by the sender), without any upper limit. An attacker can announce a huge size and use up the memory of the server with a single request.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Refuse sizes that are too large before you reserve the memory: compare the value with a fixed maximum, for example if (declaredLength > MaxAllowedSize) throw new ArgumentException(...), and answer with an error.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unbounded_allocation_from_input.benefit: One request can no longer use up all the memory of your server.

uncontrolled_format_string.title: The String.Format template is not written in the code
uncontrolled_format_string.risk: String.Format takes its template (the text with {0}, {1} markers) from the request or from a computed value. Whoever controls that text can make the page crash or produce misleading text in pages and logs.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Write the template as fixed text in the code and pass the outside value as an argument: String.Format("{0}: {1}", label, data).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

uncontrolled_format_string.benefit: Outside text can no longer change how your messages are built.

unmanaged_resource_leak_on_error.title: A stream or image is opened without using, so an error leaves it open
unmanaged_resource_leak_on_error.risk: FileStream, MemoryStream, Bitmap and similar objects hold files or system memory until Dispose() is called. Without using, an error in the next lines skips that call, and repeated errors can lock files or exhaust memory.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Declare the object with using, as in using var stream = new MemoryStream(fileBytes).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unmanaged_resource_leak_on_error.benefit: Files and memory are released even when an error occurs.

unsafe_deserialization_delegate.title: Received data is rebuilt with BinaryFormatter or a similar formatter
unsafe_deserialization_delegate.risk: BinaryFormatter, SoapFormatter and ObjectStateFormatter rebuild objects of any .NET type named in the data, including types that run code while being created. Whoever controls the data can run their own code on your server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Replace these formatters with System.Text.Json and read into a fixed type (JsonSerializer.Deserialize<MyExpectedType>(stream)); for a compact binary format, choose MessagePack or Protobuf with fixed message classes.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unsafe_deserialization_delegate.benefit: Received data can no longer make your server run code.

use_after_dispose.title: An object is used after Dispose() was called on it
use_after_dispose.risk: After Dispose(), the object has released its file, memory or connection. Using it again throws an ObjectDisposedException or, with native resources (memory handled outside .NET), can crash the program or corrupt data.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Add return or throw right after Dispose(), or move Dispose() after the last use of the object.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

use_after_dispose.benefit: The program never touches a released object.

xml_injection_csharp.title: XML text from the request is parsed directly
xml_injection_csharp.risk: XElement.Parse or XmlDocument reads XML text taken straight from the request. A visitor can add or change elements and alter data your program trusts, such as a role or a price.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Build the XML in code with new XElement(...) and put the request values in as text, never as XML to parse.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

xml_injection_csharp.benefit: Visitors can no longer change the structure of your XML data.

xxe_xmldocument.title: XmlDocument reads received XML without turning off external references
xxe_xmldocument.risk: This XmlDocument reads data from the request or a stream, or uses an XmlUrlResolver, so it follows references to outside files and addresses. A crafted document can then read files on the server or make it call other machines.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Create the document with XmlResolver = null: new XmlDocument { XmlResolver = null }.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

xxe_xmldocument.benefit: An XML document can no longer read your server's files.

zip_slip_csharp.title: A zip entry name decides where a file is written
zip_slip_csharp.risk: The path of a file inside the archive (entry.FullName) is joined to the target folder without a check. A name like ../../app/web.config writes outside that folder and can replace your program's files.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Check the final path before writing: 1) compute it with Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(destDir, entry.FullName)); 2) reject the entry if it does not start with Path.GetFullPath(destDir).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

zip_slip_csharp.benefit: An archive can no longer write files outside the folder you chose.

data_uri_html_tag.title: A link or an image loads HTML hidden in its address
data_uri_html_tag.risk: A src or href attribute starts with data:text/html, so the browser runs the page hidden in that address. An attacker can use it to make your page run their own code.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Replace this data:text/html address with a link to a real file of your site, and never accept a data: address coming from a visitor.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

data_uri_html_tag.benefit: Your pages do not run code hidden in an address.

dom_clobbering.title: An id or name in the page hides a browser variable
dom_clobbering.risk: An HTML element has an id or a name such as location or document. The browser confuses it with its own variables, which can divert your JavaScript and allow an attack.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Rename this id or name with a name specific to your page, for example location-block instead of location.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

dom_clobbering.benefit: Your JavaScript uses the browser's variables, not an element of the page.

inline_event_handler_html.title: JavaScript written directly in the HTML (onclick=…)
inline_event_handler_html.risk: An attribute such as onclick holds JavaScript directly in the HTML. The browser can then no longer block scripts that an attacker would manage to inject into the page.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Move this code into a .js file: 1) give the element an id; 2) in the .js file, add element.addEventListener('click', …); 3) remove the onclick attribute from the HTML.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

inline_event_handler_html.benefit: The browser can block any script that does not come from your files.

javascript_uri_html.title: A link runs JavaScript (javascript:…)
javascript_uri_html.risk: An href, action or src attribute starts with javascript: and the browser runs this code on click or on load. If part of it comes from a visitor, an attacker can make your page run their own code.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Replace javascript: with a real address (/, # or https://…) and put the action in a .js file with addEventListener().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

javascript_uri_html.benefit: Your links can no longer be used to run code.

arithmetic_extreme_values.title: A calculation uses the largest or smallest possible integer
arithmetic_extreme_values.risk: The code adds, subtracts or multiplies with Integer.MAX_VALUE, MIN_VALUE or their Long and Short equivalents. Java does not report the overflow: MAX_VALUE + 1 silently becomes a large negative number. Used as a size, an amount or an index, this wrong value breaks checks or data.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use Math.addExact, Math.subtractExact or Math.multiplyExact, which stop with an error instead of overflowing, or do the calculation in long or BigInteger when the result can exceed the limit.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

arithmetic_extreme_values.benefit: A calculation that goes past the limit stops with an error instead of giving a wrong value.

arithmetic_tainted.title: A number from the request is used without checking its range
arithmetic_tainted.risk: A number read from the request with Integer.parseInt() is used without checking its limits. Calculations with it can overflow (exceed the largest value an int holds and wrap to a negative one), giving a wrong size, index or amount.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Check the number before using it: 1) reject values outside the expected range with an IllegalArgumentException; 2) compute with Math.multiplyExact() or Math.addExact(), which stop on overflow instead of wrapping.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

arithmetic_tainted.benefit: A number sent by a user can no longer break your calculations.

arithmetic_uncontrolled.title: A setting value is used in a calculation without checking its range
arithmetic_uncontrolled.risk: A number read from a system property, an environment variable or a configuration file is used in a calculation without checking its limits. A wrong or very large value can overflow (wrap to a negative number) and give a wrong size, count or amount.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Check the value before computing with it: 1) reject values outside the expected range, for example with an IllegalStateException at startup; 2) compute with Math.multiplyExact() or Math.addExact(), which stop on overflow.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

arithmetic_uncontrolled.benefit: A wrong setting stops the program clearly instead of corrupting its calculations.

array_construction_tainted.title: An array is created with a size sent by the user
array_construction_tainted.risk: The size of a new array comes straight from the request, with no upper limit. A request asking for two billion items fills the memory and stops the application for every user.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Check the size before creating the array: reject the request if it is below 0 or above a maximum you set (if (size < 0 || size > MAX_SIZE) throw new IllegalArgumentException()).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

array_construction_tainted.benefit: A single request can no longer fill the server's memory.

array_index_validation.title: An array position comes straight from the user's request
array_index_validation.risk: The code reads an array at a position sent in the request, without checking it. A wrong number makes the request crash with ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, and a valid one gives access to any item of the array, even one not meant for this user.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Check the position before reading: reject the request if it is below 0 or not smaller than the array length (if (idx < 0 || idx >= items.length) throw new IllegalArgumentException()).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

array_index_validation.benefit: A request can only reach the array positions you allow.

auth_check_fail_open_on_exception.title: Access is granted when the login check fails with an error
auth_check_fail_open_on_exception.risk: When checking a user or token throws an error, the catch block lets the request go on (chain.doFilter, next.handle or continue) instead of refusing it. A malformed token or an outage of the login service then opens access to anyone.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Refuse the request on any error during the check: 1) in the catch block, answer with response.sendError(401) and stop there; 2) call chain.doFilter(request, response) only inside the try block, after the check has passed.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

auth_check_fail_open_on_exception.benefit: An error during the check always ends in a refusal, never in open access.

authz_bypass_raw_uri_check.title: An access check compares the raw address of the request
authz_bypass_raw_uri_check.risk: The code decides access by comparing request.getRequestURI(), the address exactly as the visitor typed it. Tricks such as a double slash, ";" or %2e (an encoded dot) change the text but still reach the protected page, so the check is skipped.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Compare the cleaned path, not the raw address: 1) use request.getServletPath() or StringUtils.cleanPath(request.getRequestURI()); 2) reject any request whose address contains ";" or "%2e" before the check.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

authz_bypass_raw_uri_check.benefit: A disguised address can no longer get around your access check.

cleartext_storage_class.title: A password or secret is kept in a String field
cleartext_storage_class.risk: A field of type String holds a password, token or key. Java cannot erase a String from memory, so the secret stays readable in memory dumps (copies of the program's memory saved for debugging) long after use.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Keep the secret in a character array and erase it after use: 1) declare the field as private char[] password;; 2) once you are done with it, call Arrays.fill(password, (char) 0).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cleartext_storage_class.benefit: The secret disappears from memory as soon as it is no longer needed.

cleartext_storage_cookie.title: A secret is stored in clear text in a cookie
cleartext_storage_cookie.risk: The code creates a cookie named password, token or secret that holds the value itself. The cookie is kept by the browser and sent with every request, so it can be read on the computer, in logs or by a malicious script.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Keep the secret on the server: 1) store it in the server session; 2) put only a random session identifier in the cookie, with setHttpOnly(true) and setSecure(true).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cleartext_storage_cookie.benefit: The secret never leaves your server.

cleartext_storage_properties.title: A password is written in the code of a Properties object
cleartext_storage_properties.risk: A password, key or token is written as text in a setProperty() call. Anyone who can read the code, its history or the compiled .class files gets it, and changing it requires a new release.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove the value from the code: 1) read it from an environment variable (System.getenv("DB_PASSWORD")) or a secrets manager; 2) change the password, since the old one stays in the history.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cleartext_storage_properties.benefit: The new password never appears in the code or its history.

command_injection_java_broad.title: A system command runs in a file that reads web request data
command_injection_java_broad.risk: This file starts system commands (programs run on the server) and also reads data sent by visitors. If that data ends up in a command, a visitor can run any program on your server, read your files or delete them.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Check each command of the file: 1) pass the program and each argument separately to new ProcessBuilder("ping", "-c", "1", host), never through sh -c or a joined string; 2) accept only expected values, for example a host name made of letters, digits, dots and dashes.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

command_injection_java_broad.benefit: Visitor data can no longer start programs on your server.

comparison_wider_type.title: A loop counter is compared with the size of an array or list
comparison_wider_type.risk: The loop counts up to length or size() of an array or list. If the counter has a smaller type than that size, such as short or byte, it wraps around to a negative value before reaching it. The loop then never ends and blocks the program.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Declare the loop counter as int, never as short or byte, or go through the items with a for-each loop: for (Item item : items).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

comparison_wider_type.benefit: Every loop over an array or list ends normally.

conditional_bypass_java.title: Access is granted because of a value sent by the user
conditional_bypass_java.risk: An if test on a value from the request, such as request.getParameter("admin"), decides whether to log the user in or grant access. Anyone can add that value to their request and get in without a password.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Decide access only from data the server controls: 1) check the password against your user database; 2) keep the result in the server session and read the user's role from there.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

conditional_bypass_java.benefit: Only users who really logged in get access.

dangerous_function_java.title: Runtime.exec() runs a command built with the user's input
dangerous_function_java.risk: A value from the request goes into the command passed to Runtime.exec(). An attacker can slip in extra options or another program, and run it on your server with the application's rights.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Run the program with ProcessBuilder and check the value: 1) pass the program and each argument separately (new ProcessBuilder("convert", file, "output.png")); 2) accept the value only if it is in a list of allowed names.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

dangerous_function_java.benefit: The user's input can no longer change which program runs or with which options.

db_error_exposed_java.title: Error details are sent back in the web response
db_error_exposed_java.risk: The response sent to the visitor contains getMessage(), toString() or the stack trace (the list of functions in progress) of an exception. These details can reveal table and column names, SQL queries, library versions or file paths, which help an attacker plan an attack.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Separate what you log from what you show: 1) record the full error on the server with log.error("Database error", e); 2) send the visitor only a status 500 and a generic message such as "An internal error occurred"; 3) to do it once for the whole application, use a @ControllerAdvice class with @ExceptionHandler methods.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

db_error_exposed_java.benefit: Visitors no longer learn how your database and application are built.

db_superuser_connection_java.title: The database connection uses an administrator account
db_superuser_connection_java.risk: The connection logs in to the database with an administrator account such as root, sa or postgres. If an attacker takes control of the application, they can read, change or delete every table, not just the ones it needs.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Use a dedicated account: 1) create a database user that can only read and write the application's tables; 2) read its name and password from environment variables (System.getenv("DB_PASSWORD")) instead of the address.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

db_superuser_connection_java.benefit: An attacker who takes over the application only reaches the tables it uses.

db_tls_disabled_java.title: The database connection is not encrypted (Java)
db_tls_disabled_java.risk: The JDBC address turns off TLS (the encryption of the connection) with useSSL=false, sslMode=DISABLED or ssl=false, or skips the server certificate check. Anyone on the network can read queries, results and the database password, or pose as the server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Turn encryption on and keep the certificate check: 1) in the JDBC address, write useSSL=true&requireSSL=true&verifyServerCertificate=true for MySQL or sslmode=verify-full for PostgreSQL; 2) add the server certificate to the Java truststore (the list of certificates Java trusts).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

db_tls_disabled_java.benefit: Traffic between the application and the database can no longer be read on the network.

exec_relative_path.title: A command is started by its name alone, without its full path
exec_relative_path.risk: Runtime.exec() receives a program name such as "convert" without its full path, so the system searches the folders listed in the PATH variable. Anyone who can change PATH or drop a file in one of those folders can make your code run their own program.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Give the full path of the program and pass each argument separately: new ProcessBuilder("/usr/bin/convert", "image.png", "output.jpg").start().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

exec_relative_path.benefit: Your code always runs the program you chose.

exec_tainted_environment.title: A command is built from an environment variable or the request
exec_tainted_environment.risk: Runtime.exec() or ProcessBuilder receives a value from System.getenv(), System.getProperty() or the request. Whoever can set that value, through the server settings, a container or a request, chooses the program your application runs.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Write the program's full path in the code and check the value: 1) accept it only if it is in a list of allowed values; 2) pass it as a separate argument (new ProcessBuilder("/usr/bin/backup", "--mode", mode)).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

exec_tainted_environment.benefit: Your application only runs the programs you chose.

exec_unescaped.title: The command given to Runtime.exec() is built by gluing text together
exec_unescaped.risk: The command passed to Runtime.exec() is assembled with +. If one of the pieces comes from a user or a file name, they can add options or arguments of their own and change what the program does.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Pass the program and each argument as separate items: new ProcessBuilder("ffmpeg", "-i", userFile, "output.mp4").start().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

exec_unescaped.benefit: Each value stays a single argument and cannot add new ones.

groovy_injection.title: A Groovy script is run from text that may come from a user
groovy_injection.risk: The code runs a Groovy script with GroovyShell, GroovyClassLoader or GroovyScriptEngine. If the script text comes from a user, they can read files, start programs and take over the server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Never run a script written by a user: let them choose from scripts you wrote yourself, or use a formula engine limited to calculations.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

groovy_injection.benefit: No code sent by a user runs on your server.

hardcoded_connection_string_java.title: A database password is written in the code (Java)
hardcoded_connection_string_java.risk: DriverManager.getConnection() receives the password as text, or the jdbc: address contains a user name and password before the @. Anyone who can read the code or its history can log in to the database.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Remove the password from the code: 1) read the address and the password from environment variables (System.getenv("DB_PASSWORD")) or a secrets manager; 2) change the password, since the old one stays in the history.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

hardcoded_connection_string_java.benefit: The new password never appears in the code or its history.

http_response_splitting.title: A response header is filled with a value from the request
http_response_splitting.risk: addHeader(), setHeader(), addCookie() or sendRedirect() receives a value straight from the request. If it holds line breaks, an attacker can add headers or a whole fake page to the response, for example to steal another visitor's session.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Clean the value before putting it in the response: 1) remove the line breaks (CR and LF characters) or reject the request; 2) for sendRedirect(), accept only addresses from a list you set.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

http_response_splitting.benefit: A visitor can no longer change the structure of your responses.

http_smuggling_trailer_trust.title: Trailers (headers sent after the body) are copied as normal headers
http_smuggling_trailer_trust.risk: In a request sent in pieces (chunked), trailers are headers that come after the body. The code copies them into the main headers unchecked, so an attacker can add a header that the proxy in front of your application never checked.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Keep trailers apart from the headers: 1) store them in a separate map, never in the one used for security decisions; 2) accept only the trailer names in a list you set, and never let one replace an existing header.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

http_smuggling_trailer_trust.benefit: Your security checks see the same headers as the proxy in front of them.

infinite_loop_user_input.title: The end of a loop depends on a value sent by the user
infinite_loop_user_input.risk: The stop condition of a loop reads a value from the request. An attacker can send a huge number, or a value that is never reached, and keep the server busy for a very long time, slowing it down for everyone.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Bound the loop: 1) read the value once before the loop and reject it if it is above a maximum you set; 2) add a counter that stops the loop after a fixed number of rounds.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

infinite_loop_user_input.benefit: A single request can no longer keep your server busy indefinitely.

insecure_basic_auth.title: Login details are sent over HTTP, without encryption
insecure_basic_auth.risk: The connection sends a user name and password to an http:// address, which is not encrypted. Anyone on the network, a public Wi-Fi for example, can read them and log in in your place.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Send login details only over https: 1) replace http:// with https:// in the address; 2) pass them in the Authorization header rather than in the address, where they end up in logs.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_basic_auth.benefit: Login details can no longer be read on the network.

insecure_bean_validation.title: A validation message contains an expression that can run code
insecure_bean_validation.risk: The message of a @Pattern, @Size or @NotNull annotation holds a ${…} expression or a value from the request. Bean Validation evaluates these expressions, so a value chosen by a user can run code on the server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Write fixed messages: use a key from a message file (message = "{validation.invalid.value}") and never put ${…} or a request value in it.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_bean_validation.benefit: Validation messages can no longer run code.

insecure_cookie_flag.title: A cookie may be sent without encryption (setSecure(false))
insecure_cookie_flag.risk: With setSecure(false), the browser also sends this cookie over plain HTTP, without encryption. Someone on the same network, for example on public Wi-Fi, can read it and, if it is a session cookie, log in as the user.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Protect the cookie: 1) replace setSecure(false) with cookie.setSecure(true); 2) add cookie.setHttpOnly(true) so that page scripts cannot read it.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_cookie_flag.benefit: The cookie only travels encrypted, over HTTPS.

insecure_javamail.title: JavaMail sends the mail password without encryption
insecure_javamail.risk: mail.smtp.auth is set to true, but neither mail.smtp.starttls.enable nor mail.smtp.ssl.enable is turned on nearby. The user name and password of the mail account then travel in clear text, and anyone on the network can read them.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Encrypt the mail connection: add props.put("mail.smtp.starttls.enable", "true") with port 587, or props.put("mail.smtp.ssl.enable", "true") with port 465.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_javamail.benefit: The mail password can no longer be read on the network.

insecure_ldap_auth.title: An LDAP directory is reached with ldap://, without encryption
insecure_ldap_auth.risk: The code connects to an LDAP directory (the server that checks user names and passwords) through an ldap:// address, which is not encrypted. The passwords sent to log in travel in clear text, and anyone on the network can capture and reuse them.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Encrypt the directory connection: use an ldaps:// address (port 636), or start TLS on the connection before sending the password.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_ldap_auth.benefit: Directory passwords can no longer be read on the network.

insecure_maven_dependency.title: A Maven repository is declared with http://, without encryption
insecure_maven_dependency.risk: A <repository> block uses an http:// address, so libraries are downloaded without encryption. Someone on the network can swap a .jar for a malicious one, which then runs inside your build and your application.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Replace http:// with https:// in every <url> of your repositories, and remove those that do not offer https (Maven 3.8.1 and later block http repositories by default).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_maven_dependency.benefit: The libraries you download are the ones the repository published.

insufficient_key_size_java.title: An RSA or DSA key is too short (Java)
insufficient_key_size_java.risk: The key generator is set to 512, 768 or 1024 bits with initialize(). Keys this short can be broken with enough computing power, which lets an attacker read the protected data or forge signatures.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Generate longer keys: call initialize(2048) at least, or 3072 for keys kept for years, or switch to elliptic-curve keys (KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC")).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insufficient_key_size_java.benefit: Your keys resist the computing power available today.

jexl_injection.title: A JEXL expression is built from a value sent by the user
jexl_injection.risk: A value from the request reaches createExpression() or createScript() of JEXL (a formula language for Java). JEXL can call any Java method, so the user can start programs or read files on the server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Never build an expression from what the user sends: let them choose an expression you wrote yourself (TRUSTED_FORMULAS.get(formulaId)), and limit what JEXL may call with JexlPermissions.RESTRICTED.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

jexl_injection.benefit: No formula sent by a user can run code on your server.

ldap_injection_java_broad.title: An LDAP search runs in a file that reads web request data
ldap_injection_java_broad.risk: This file searches an LDAP directory (the server that stores users and groups) and also reads data sent by visitors. If that data is glued into the search filter, a visitor can see other users' details or get around a login check.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Put a placeholder in the filter and pass the value apart: ctx.search(base, "(uid={0})", new Object[]{ username }, controls), which escapes the special characters for you; with Spring, use LdapQueryBuilder.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

ldap_injection_java_broad.benefit: Visitor data can no longer change your directory searches.

lock_order_inconsistency.title: Two locks are taken in opposite orders, which can freeze threads
lock_order_inconsistency.risk: One block of code takes lock A then lock B with synchronized, another takes B then A. If two threads (tasks running at the same time) each hold one lock and wait for the other, both stay blocked forever and the application stops responding.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Take the locks in a single order: 1) pick one, for example lockA before lockB, and follow it in every synchronized block; 2) where that is hard, use ReentrantLock.tryLock() with a time limit.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

lock_order_inconsistency.benefit: Threads can no longer block each other forever.

log4shell_jndi.title: The Log4Shell attack text ${jndi: appears in the code
log4shell_jndi.risk: A text starting with ${jndi: is the form of the Log4Shell attack (CVE-2021-44228). When Log4j before version 2.17.1 writes such a text to a log, it can download and run code chosen by the attacker on your server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Update Log4j and remove the text: 1) set log4j-core to version 2.17.1 or later in pom.xml or build.gradle; 2) delete this ${jndi: text, or keep it only in a test that checks the update.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

log4shell_jndi.benefit: A log line can no longer make your server run someone else's code.

mass_assignment_java.title: Every request parameter is copied onto an object
mass_assignment_java.risk: BeanUtils.copyProperties() or populate() copies every parameter of the request onto an object, including fields the user should not touch. By adding a parameter such as role=admin or balance=1000, a user can change them.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Copy only the allowed fields: 1) create a DTO (a class with just the fields the user may set); 2) fill it from the request field by field, then copy it with BeanUtils.copyProperties(dto, userEntity).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

mass_assignment_java.benefit: Users can only change the fields you allow.

missing_jwt_signature_check.title: A JWT token is read without checking its signature
missing_jwt_signature_check.risk: A JWT (a signed token that says who the user is) is read with Jwts.parser() without a key to check its signature. Anyone can then write a token that claims to be another user or an administrator, and the application accepts it.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Give the key and read the token with parseClaimsJws(), which rejects a token with a wrong signature: Jwts.parserBuilder().setSigningKey(signingKey).build().parseClaimsJws(token).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

missing_jwt_signature_check.benefit: Only tokens signed with your key are accepted.

missing_permission_check_java.title: A Jenkins web action runs without checking permissions
missing_permission_check_java.risk: This doXxx() method receives a StaplerRequest, so Jenkins makes it reachable at a web address, but it does not call checkPermission() at its start. Any user who can reach that address can run the action, even without the right to do so.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Call the permission check on the first line of the method, before any change: getTarget().checkPermission(Item.CONFIGURE).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

missing_permission_check_java.benefit: Only users with the right permission can run the action.

mvel_injection.title: Text from a request is run as an MVEL expression
mvel_injection.risk: A value from an HTTP request reaches MVEL.eval() or a similar call, which runs it as an MVEL expression (a small language that can call any Java code). The sender can run commands on your server, read its files or take control of it.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Never evaluate text sent by a user: 1) keep the allowed expressions in your code; 2) let the request only choose one by name, as in MVEL.eval(TRUSTED_EXPRESSIONS.get(exprId), vars).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

mvel_injection.benefit: A request can no longer run code on your server.

netty_bytebuf_leak_on_error.title: A Netty buffer kept with retain() is not released if an error occurs
netty_bytebuf_leak_on_error.risk: The code keeps a Netty buffer (a block of memory reused between requests) with retain(), but no release() or try/finally follows nearby. If processing fails, the memory is never given back, and repeated bad messages can exhaust it and stop the server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Release the buffer in every case: put the code that uses it in a try block and call ReferenceCountUtil.release(buffer) in the finally block.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

netty_bytebuf_leak_on_error.benefit: The server gives memory back even when a message is malformed.

netty_response_splitting.title: A Netty response header is filled with a value from the request
netty_response_splitting.risk: A response header (a line of information sent before the page) gets a value taken from the request. If that value holds a line break, the sender can add their own headers or even a fake page. This can set a cookie in the visitor's browser or poison a cache (a stored copy of pages served to others).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove the line break characters (CR and LF) from the value before putting it in a header, or reject the request when the value contains one.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

netty_response_splitting.benefit: A request can no longer add headers or content to your responses.

nosql_document_parse_java.title: A MongoDB filter is built from a text with Document.parse()
nosql_document_parse_java.risk: Document.parse() or BasicDBObject.parse() turns a variable text into a MongoDB query. If that text comes from a user, they can add operators such as $where or $ne, for example to log in without a password or read other people's data.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Build the filter in code with the Filters class, one field at a time, and pass the user's value only as a value: Filters.eq("username", username).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

nosql_document_parse_java.benefit: A user's value can no longer change what your queries look for.

numeric_cast_tainted.title: A number from the request is forced into a smaller type with (int)
numeric_cast_tainted.risk: A number read from the request as a long or double is converted to int, short or byte with a cast. Java silently cuts values that do not fit: 2147483648 becomes -2147483648, which gives a negative index, a wrong count or a wrong amount.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Convert safely: 1) use Math.toIntExact(), which stops with an error when the value does not fit; 2) reject values outside the expected range with an IllegalArgumentException.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

numeric_cast_tainted.benefit: A number sent by a user can no longer change sign or size without warning.

ognl_injection.title: Text from a request is run as an OGNL expression
ognl_injection.risk: A value from an HTTP request is given to Ognl.getValue() or a similar call, which runs it as OGNL (a small Struts language that can call any Java code). This is how the major attacks on Struts worked: the sender can run commands on your server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Never evaluate text sent by a user: 1) check the requested field name against a fixed list (ALLOWED_FIELDS); 2) read the field with PropertyUtils.getProperty(bean, propName); 3) keep Struts up to date.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

ognl_injection.benefit: A request can no longer run code on your server.

partial_path_traversal.title: A folder check with startsWith() forgets the final separator
partial_path_traversal.risk: The code checks that a file is inside a folder by comparing paths with startsWith(), without a separator at the end. A path such as /safe/dir-evil/secret passes the check for /safe/dir, so a user can read or write files in a neighbouring folder.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Add the separator to the folder path before comparing: file.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(baseDir.getCanonicalPath() + File.separator).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

partial_path_traversal.benefit: Only files really inside the folder pass the check.

password_reversible_storage_java.title: A password is encrypted, so it can be decrypted (Java)
password_reversible_storage_java.risk: The code encrypts a password with Cipher, so it can be decrypted. Whoever gets the key can turn every stored password back into clear text and try it on other sites.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Store a hash (a fingerprint of the password that cannot be reversed) rather than an encrypted copy: use BCryptPasswordEncoder from Spring Security, Argon2 or PBKDF2, and check logins with matches().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

password_reversible_storage_java.benefit: A leak of the database no longer reveals the passwords.

path_traversal_fis.title: Files are opened by code that also reads outside data
path_traversal_fis.risk: This source file opens files with FileInputStream, FileOutputStream, FileReader or FileWriter, and also reads outside data: request parameters, headers, cookies, environment variables. If that data forms the path, a visitor can write ../../ to reach any file on the server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Keep every path inside an allowed folder: 1) build it with Path p = base.resolve(name).normalize(); 2) refuse it if p.startsWith(base) is false, otherwise open p.toFile().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

path_traversal_fis.benefit: Visitors can reach only the files of the allowed folder.

polynomial_redos_java.title: A regular expression can freeze the server on some inputs
polynomial_redos_java.risk: Pattern.compile receives a regular expression (a search pattern for text) with nested repetitions, such as (a+)* or .*.*. On a long, well-chosen text, Java tries an enormous number of combinations and the processor stays busy for minutes, so your service stops answering.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Make the expression safe: 1) rewrite it without a repetition inside another, for example a*b instead of (a+)*b, or use a possessive form such as a++ that never goes back; 2) limit the length of the text you check with it.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

polynomial_redos_java.benefit: No text, however crafted, can block your service through this expression.

predictable_seed.title: SecureRandom is started from a fixed or guessable seed
predictable_seed.risk: The seed (the starting value of the random number generator) is a fixed text, a number or the current time. Depending on the Java platform, someone who guesses it can predict the generated values, such as session tokens, reset codes or keys.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Create the generator without an argument, new SecureRandom(), so that Java takes its seed from the operating system.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

predictable_seed.benefit: Your tokens and keys can no longer be guessed from the seed.

regex_injection_java.title: Text from a request is compiled as a regular expression
regex_injection_java.risk: Pattern.compile() receives a value from the request, so the user writes the regular expression (a search pattern for text). Some patterns take hours to test against a text, which blocks the server's processor and makes the site unavailable.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Treat the user's text as plain text to look for: Pattern.compile(Pattern.quote(userInput)), or use String.contains() when no pattern is needed.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

regex_injection_java.benefit: A search sent by a user can no longer block your server.

rsa_without_oaep.title: RSA encryption uses the old PKCS#1 v1.5 padding instead of OAEP
rsa_without_oaep.risk: Cipher.getInstance("RSA") uses PKCS#1 v1.5 padding (the filler bytes added to the data before encryption) by default. If your server reports whether a decryption failed, an attacker can recover the encrypted data by sending many altered messages (the Bleichenbacher attack).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use OAEP padding: Cipher.getInstance("RSA/ECB/OAEPWithSHA-256AndMGF1Padding"), with the same setting on the side that decrypts.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

rsa_without_oaep.benefit: Encrypted data can no longer be recovered through error messages.

session_fixation_java.title: The session number is not renewed after login
session_fixation_java.risk: After login, the code keeps the session number (the identifier that keeps a user logged in) it had before. An attacker who planted or saw that number beforehand, through a link or a shared computer, is then logged in as the victim.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Call request.changeSessionId() right after a successful login, before saving the user in the session; with Spring Security, keep its default protection against this problem turned on.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

session_fixation_java.benefit: A session number known before login is useless to an attacker.

socket_auth_race.title: Data is read from a connection before the client is authenticated
socket_auth_race.risk: After accept(), the server reads data from the socket (the network connection) before calling authenticate(). Data sent by a client who has not proved its identity is then processed, which can let it act without logging in.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Authenticate the client before reading anything: call authenticate() right after accept() and close the socket when it fails.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

socket_auth_race.benefit: The server only processes data from authenticated clients.

spring_actuator_exposed.title: All Spring Actuator admin pages are open to the network
spring_actuator_exposed.risk: The line management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=* publishes every Actuator page (built-in pages to inspect a running Spring application). The page /actuator/env shows the configuration and its secrets, and /actuator/heapdump gives a copy of the memory, passwords included.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Open only what you need: 1) set management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health,info; 2) protect the other Actuator pages with Spring Security so that only administrators reach them.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

spring_actuator_exposed.benefit: Your configuration and memory are no longer readable from the network.

sql_injection_java_broad.title: An SQL query runs in a file that reads web request data
sql_injection_java_broad.risk: This file runs SQL queries (the commands sent to the database) and also reads data sent by visitors, such as form fields or headers. If that data is glued into a query, a visitor can read, change or delete your data.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Check each query of the file: 1) write a ? in the SQL text where each value goes, with conn.prepareStatement("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?"); 2) pass the values with setString or setInt, never by joining them to the text with +.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

sql_injection_java_broad.benefit: Visitor data can no longer change your SQL queries.

static_initialization_vector.title: The encryption reuses a fixed starting value (IV) written in the code
static_initialization_vector.risk: The IV (a random starting value that must change with every encryption) is fixed in the code. The same message then always gives the same encrypted result, which leaks patterns, and with AES-GCM an attacker can even forge messages.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Draw a new IV for every encryption: 1) fill a byte array with new SecureRandom().nextBytes(iv); 2) store the IV next to the encrypted data so you can decrypt it later.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

static_initialization_vector.benefit: Two identical messages no longer give the same encrypted result.

stored_procedure_dynamic_java.title: A stored procedure call is built by joining text with +
stored_procedure_dynamic_java.risk: A call to a stored procedure (a program saved in the database) is built by joining an EXEC or CALL text with values using +. If a value comes from a user, that user can add their own SQL, for example to read or delete all data.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Call the procedure with prepareCall(), a ? for each argument, and pass the values separately: conn.prepareCall("{call GetUser(?)}"), then cs.setString(1, userName).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

stored_procedure_dynamic_java.benefit: A value from a user can no longer change your queries.

taint_sensitive_attr_write.title: Sensitive attribute set from user input
taint_sensitive_attr_write.risk: An attacker can manipulate role or permission attributes by injecting crafted values, leading to privilege escalation and unauthorized access to restricted functionality.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Set rights fields only from your own administration code, never from the request, and when the visitor may choose, accept only a value from a fixed list.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_sensitive_attr_write.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_trust_boundary.title: A value from the request is stored in the session without being checked
taint_trust_boundary.risk: The session holds what the server trusts about a visitor, such as their identity or role. Here a value sent by the visitor goes into it unchecked, so the visitor can, for example, take the identifier of another user.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Check the value before storing it in the session: convert it to the expected type (a number, an identifier), compare it with a list of allowed values, or store a value computed by the server instead.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_trust_boundary.benefit: The session only holds values your server has checked.

tainted_permissions_check.title: The permission being checked comes from the request
tainted_permissions_check.risk: A check such as hasRole() or isPermitted() receives the role or permission to test from the request itself. The user then chooses what is checked, for example a role they already have, and gets past a control meant to stop them.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Write the permission in your code, based on the action being done: subject.isPermitted("resource:read") before a read, never a value taken from the request.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

tainted_permissions_check.benefit: Users can no longer choose which permission is checked.

temp_dir_info_disclosure.title: A file is created by hand in the shared temporary folder
temp_dir_info_disclosure.risk: The code creates a file in java.io.tmpdir, a folder that every user of the machine can usually see, often under a name easy to guess. Another user or program can then read its contents or put a file of their own in its place.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Let Java create the file: 1) call Files.createTempFile() with the permissions PosixFilePermissions.fromString("rw-------"), so that it gets a unique name and only you can read it; 2) delete the file once you no longer need it.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

temp_dir_info_disclosure.benefit: Other users of the machine can no longer read or replace your temporary files.

template_injection_java.title: A page template is built from text sent in the request
template_injection_java.risk: The text of a FreeMarker, Velocity or Thymeleaf template (a page model with fields to fill) comes from the request. Template code can call Java, so the sender can read the server's files and secrets, or run commands.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Keep the template in your files and pass the user's data only as values: 1) load it with cfg.getTemplate("email-confirm.ftl"); 2) put the data in the model, as in model.put("username", name), before template.process(model, out).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

template_injection_java.benefit: A request can no longer run code through your templates.

toctou_race_condition.title: A file is checked, then used in a separate step
toctou_race_condition.risk: The code checks that a file exists or can be read, then opens it a moment later. In between, another program or user who can write in the folder can swap the file, for example for a link to a password file.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Open or create the file directly in one step and handle the error if it fails: catch NoSuchFileException instead of calling exists() first, and create files with Files.newOutputStream(path, StandardOpenOption.CREATE_NEW).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

toctou_race_condition.benefit: Nobody can swap the file between the check and its use.

trust_boundary_java.title: A value from the request is stored in the session without checking
trust_boundary_java.risk: The code puts a value from the request into the HTTP session (data the server keeps for each user). The rest of the application usually trusts the session, so a user can set a value such as their own role.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Store in the session only values your server has checked or computed: 1) check a request value against a fixed list of allowed values; 2) take sensitive data, such as the role, from your database after login.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

trust_boundary_java.benefit: The session only holds values your server can trust.

unrestricted_file_upload_java.title: Uploaded files are saved without checking their type
unrestricted_file_upload_java.risk: The code saves an uploaded file with transferTo() or uses its original name from getOriginalFilename(), and nothing in this source file checks its type. An attacker can upload a program or a web page, then open it on your server to run their own code.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Check every upload before saving it: 1) accept only a short list of extensions, such as jpg, png and pdf, and check the real content with Files.probeContentType; 2) save the file under a random name, UUID.randomUUID() + "." + ext, in a folder the web server does not publish.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unrestricted_file_upload_java.benefit: Only harmless files of the expected type reach your server.

url_forward_injection.title: A request is forwarded to a page chosen by the user
url_forward_injection.risk: getRequestDispatcher() receives a path taken from the request, so the user chooses which internal page handles it. They can reach files and pages that are not public, such as /WEB-INF/web.xml or an admin page, without the usual checks.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Map the user's choice to a fixed list of pages and refuse anything else: dest = ALLOWED.get(page), then an error 400 when dest is null.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

url_forward_injection.benefit: Users can only reach the pages you chose.

use_ssl_socket.title: A network connection is opened without encryption (plain Socket)
use_ssl_socket.risk: The code opens a connection with new Socket(), which sends everything in clear text. Anyone on the same network, a public Wi-Fi for example, can read or change the data, passwords included.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Open an encrypted connection with TLS (the protocol behind https): create the socket with SSLSocketFactory.getDefault().createSocket(host, port) instead of new Socket(host, port).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

use_ssl_socket.benefit: Data sent over the connection can no longer be read or changed on the way.

weak_cipher_java.title: An outdated encryption method is used (DES, RC4, Blowfish…)
weak_cipher_java.risk: Cipher.getInstance() selects DES, DESede, RC2, RC4 or Blowfish, methods now known to be too weak. An attacker who gets the encrypted data can read it in clear.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Switch to AES in GCM mode: call Cipher.getInstance("AES/GCM/NoPadding") with a 256-bit key and a new random IV (starting value) for each message.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

weak_cipher_java.benefit: Your encrypted data stays unreadable to an attacker.

weak_random_java_util.title: Random values come from a predictable generator (Random, Math.random)
weak_random_java_util.risk: java.util.Random and Math.random() produce numbers that can be guessed from a few earlier ones. If they create a token, a reset code or a session number, an attacker can predict it and take over an account.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use java.security.SecureRandom wherever the value must stay secret, for example new SecureRandom().nextInt(1000000) for a code, and keep Random and Math.random() for games or tests only.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

weak_random_java_util.benefit: Codes and tokens cannot be guessed.

world_writable_file_read.title: A file is made writable by everyone, then read
world_writable_file_read.risk: setWritable(true, false) lets every account on the machine change the file, and the program then reads it. Another program or user can replace its content just before the read, and the application trusts what they wrote.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Give write access to the owner only: file.setWritable(true, true), or Files.setPosixFilePermissions() with rw------- for finer control.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

world_writable_file_read.benefit: Other accounts on the machine can no longer change what your program reads.

xpath_injection_java_eval.title: An XPath query is built with text sent by the user (Java)
xpath_injection_java_eval.risk: The XPath query (a search language for XML documents) is assembled by gluing in a value from the request. An attacker can change the query and read parts of the document they should not see, such as other users' accounts.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Pass the value as a variable instead of gluing it into the query: 1) write $name in the expression ("/users[@name=$name]"); 2) give its value through xpath.setXPathVariableResolver() before compile().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

xpath_injection_java_eval.benefit: A value sent by the user can no longer change what the query searches for.

xslt_injection.title: An XSLT transformation runs with the default, unprotected settings
xslt_injection.risk: TransformerFactory.newInstance() is used straight away, without turning on secure processing. If the stylesheet (the XSLT file that describes the transformation) comes from a user, it can call Java, read files on your server or run commands.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Set up the factory before using it: 1) call factory.setFeature(XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, true); 2) load stylesheets only from your own files, never from a request.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

xslt_injection.benefit: A stylesheet can no longer run code or read files on your server.

zip_slip.title: A ZIP entry name is used as a file path without checking it
zip_slip.risk: The path of an extracted file is built from entry.getName(), the name written inside the archive. A crafted archive can use names like ../../etc/cron.d/job to write files outside the target folder and replace programs or settings.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Check the final path before writing: 1) build it with new File(destDir, entry.getName()); 2) refuse the entry when destFile.getCanonicalPath() does not start with destDir.getCanonicalPath() + File.separator.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

zip_slip.benefit: An archive can only write files inside the folder you chose.

account_enumeration_response_differentia.title: The answer reveals whether an account exists
account_enumeration_response_differentia.risk: When the account is not found, this code answers with a 404 or 400 error, different from the answer for an existing account. By trying many email addresses, an attacker learns which ones have an account, then targets them with fake emails or by guessing their passwords.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Give the same answer in both cases, for example status 200 with "If an account exists, a link has been sent", and send the email only when the account exists.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

account_enumeration_response_differentia.benefit: Nobody can find out who has an account on your site.

angularjs_insecure_url_whitelist.title: AngularJS trusts resources from too many addresses
angularjs_insecure_url_whitelist.risk: The list passed to $sceDelegateProvider.resourceUrlWhitelist() contains a "**" wildcard, for example http://**.example.com/**. AngularJS then loads templates and scripts from any matching address, including a subdomain an attacker controls.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
List only the exact addresses you use, such as "self" and http://cdn.example.com/**, without "**" in the domain name.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

angularjs_insecure_url_whitelist.benefit: AngularJS only loads resources from your own servers.

api_key_in_url.title: API Key in URL
api_key_in_url.risk: API keys in URLs are logged by web servers, proxies, and browsers (CWE-598).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Take the key out of the address: 1) send it in a header (Authorization) instead; 2) read it from your secret configuration, not from the code; 3) replace the key, since the old one is already in logs.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

api_key_in_url.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

auth_truthy_check_ignores_error.title: Access is granted as soon as the session exists, even with an error
auth_truthy_check_ignores_error.risk: The code lets the user in as soon as the session, auth or token object exists, without checking its error field. Some login libraries return such an object even when the check failed, so access is granted anyway.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Check the error field too before letting the user in: if (session && !session.error) { … }.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

auth_truthy_check_ignores_error.benefit: A failed login check always ends with access denied.

bad_tag_filter.title: HTML tags filtered with a regex
bad_tag_filter.risk: Filtering HTML tags with regular expressions is an unreliable sanitization strategy — attackers bypass it with malformed tags (<scr<script>ipt>), nested tags, Unicode equivalents, or by breaking tags across multiple attributes. Regex-based HTML parsing is fundamentally broken (CWE-116, CWE-020, CWE-185).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Escape the text when it must show as plain text, or clean it with a maintained HTML cleaning library that keeps only the tags you allow, instead of removing tags with a pattern.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

bad_tag_filter.benefit: Ensures HTML sanitization is reliable and resistant to bypass via malformed or nested tags.

base64_eval.title: Code hidden in base64 is executed
base64_eval.risk: The program decodes a base64 text (a way to write data with plain letters) and runs it as code. This is how malicious code hides from reviewers and security tools, and whoever controls that text controls the program.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Do not run decoded text: read data with a JSON parser, and if it is code you did not write, remove it and check where it came from.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

base64_eval.benefit: No hidden code runs in your program.

base64_obfuscation.title: A long base64 text is decoded in the code
base64_obfuscation.risk: The code decodes with atob() a long base64 text (a way to write data with plain letters) written in the file. This is a common way to hide malicious code from readers, for example code that steals the visitors' cookies.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Decode the text once to see what it contains: if it is data, write it readably in the code; if it is code you did not write, remove it and check where it came from.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

base64_obfuscation.benefit: Every piece of code in your project can be read and checked.

broken_crypto_algorithm.title: Data is encrypted with an outdated algorithm (DES, RC4, Blowfish…)
broken_crypto_algorithm.risk: The code encrypts with DES, triple DES, RC2, RC4 or Blowfish through crypto.createCipher() or createCipheriv(). These algorithms are broken or too weak today, so an attacker who gets the encrypted data can often recover the original.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Switch to AES-256-GCM with a new random IV (a starting value) for each message: crypto.createCipheriv("aes-256-gcm", key, crypto.randomBytes(12)).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

broken_crypto_algorithm.benefit: Your encrypted data stays unreadable without the key.

buffer_index_without_bounds_check.title: Buffer read without bounds check
buffer_index_without_bounds_check.risk: A buffer is read at an offset derived from external/untrusted input (a request parameter, a computed index) with no visible bounds check against the buffer's actual length. An out-of-range offset causes an out-of-bounds read, potentially disclosing adjacent heap memory or crashing the process (CWE-125).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
