Validate the offset against the buffer's length before reading (offset >= 0 && offset + size <= buffer.length), and reject the request otherwise instead of letting the read proceed.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

buffer_index_without_bounds_check.benefit: Prevents out-of-bounds reads and the associated memory disclosure or crash when processing attacker-controlled offsets.

build_artifact_leak.title: The production build publishes the original source code (source maps)
build_artifact_leak.risk: The build settings produce source maps (files that link the compressed code back to the original code) for production. Anyone who visits the site can download them and read your original code, comments and internal addresses.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Turn source maps off for production: 1) set devtool: false (or sourceMap: false) when NODE_ENV is "production"; 2) if you need them to read error reports, upload them to your error tracking service and leave them out of the public files.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

build_artifact_leak.benefit: Visitors only get the compressed code, not your original source.

case_sensitive_middleware_path.title: A protection tied to one path may be bypassed with capital letters
case_sensitive_middleware_path.risk: A protection, such as a login check, is attached with app.use() to a single path like "/admin". If a server placed in front of your app, or another route, treats "/Admin" and "/admin" differently, a request with other capital letters can reach the page without the check.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Apply the protection to the router (express.Router()) that holds all the protected routes, rather than to one path, or convert every path to lower case first with req.url = req.url.toLowerCase() in a function placed before all others (app.use()).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

case_sensitive_middleware_path.benefit: The protection applies whatever capital letters the address uses.

cleartext_cookie.title: A sensitive cookie can travel without encryption (Secure missing)
cleartext_cookie.risk: This cookie holds a token or a password but is set without secure: true. The browser then also sends it over plain HTTP, where anyone on the same network, such as public Wi-Fi, can read it and log in as the user.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Add secure: true to the cookie options, with httpOnly: true and sameSite: "Strict": res.cookie("token", value, { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: "Strict" }).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cleartext_cookie.benefit: The cookie only travels over encrypted connections.

cleartext_logging.title: A password or token is written to the logs
cleartext_logging.risk: A console or logger call writes a value whose name looks secret, such as password, token or api_key. Logs are kept for a long time and read by many people and tools, so the secret leaks to all of them.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove the secret from the message: log only that it is present (token present: true) or its last characters, never the value itself.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cleartext_logging.benefit: Reading the logs no longer reveals your secrets.

cleartext_storage_sensitive.title: A password or token is stored in clear
cleartext_storage_sensitive.risk: A password, token or secret is saved as plain text, in a file or in the storage of the browser (localStorage). Any program, script or person who can read that place gets the secret.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Keep secrets out of plain storage: keep them on the server or in your secret manager, or encrypt them before writing and keep the key elsewhere.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cleartext_storage_sensitive.benefit: Reading the stored data no longer reveals your secrets.

client_side_ssrf.title: The browser sends a request to an address taken from the page URL
client_side_ssrf.risk: The address given to fetch() or axios comes from the page address, document.referrer or the page content, which an attacker can set in a link. The browser then sends the request, sometimes with the user's login data, to a server the attacker chooses.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Accept only addresses from your own list: read the value with URLSearchParams, then send the request only if it is in that list.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

client_side_ssrf.benefit: The browser only sends requests to the servers you chose.

conditional_bypass.title: Access is granted based on a value the visitor sends
conditional_bypass.risk: The code grants rights when a field of the request, such as req.body.role, equals "admin" or true. The visitor writes that request, so they only need to send that value to get the access.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Read the role from a trusted source on the server, such as the session or the user record in your database, never from the request.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

conditional_bypass.benefit: A visitor cannot give themselves rights by changing the request.

cors_credentials_wildcard.title: CORS allows every site and sends credentials at the same time
cors_credentials_wildcard.risk: The CORS settings (the rules that let other sites call your server from a browser) combine credentials: true with origin: "*" or origin: true. Browsers refuse "*" with credentials, and origin: true echoes back any origin, which lets every site act with your users' cookies.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Name the sites you trust in origin, for example cors({ origin: "https://app.example.com", credentials: true }), and never echo back any origin.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cors_credentials_wildcard.benefit: Only the sites you name can call your server with your users' cookies.

cross_tenant_resource_access.title: A record is fetched by its ID without checking its organization
cross_tenant_resource_access.risk: In an app shared by several organizations, this query looks up a record by its identifier only, without the caller's workspaceId or organizationId. Any logged-in user who changes the identifier in the address can read or modify another organization's data.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Add the user's organization to the query: findOne({ _id: req.params.id, workspaceId: req.user.workspaceId }), and answer 404 when nothing is found.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cross_tenant_resource_access.benefit: Each organization only sees and changes its own data.

crud_without_ownership.title: CRUD without ownership check
crud_without_ownership.risk: Users can access or modify resources belonging to other users (IDOR).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Verify resource ownership before every CRUD operation.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

crud_without_ownership.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

data_uri_html.title: An HTML page is built into a data: address
data_uri_html.risk: A data:text/html address carries a whole HTML page, scripts included, inside the address itself. Opened in a frame or a window, this page runs its scripts in the user's browser, and anyone who controls part of it controls those scripts.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Point to a real file on your server, such as /images/photo.jpg, and never build data:text/html addresses.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

data_uri_html.benefit: No HTML page hidden in an address can run scripts in your site.

db_connection_string_credentials_js.title: A database address with its password is written in the code
db_connection_string_credentials_js.risk: This database address contains a user name and a password (user:password@host). Anyone who can read the code or its history, now or later, can connect to the database with it.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Remove the address from the code: 1) read it from an environment variable (process.env.DATABASE_URL) or from your secret manager; 2) change the database password, since the old one stays in the history.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

db_connection_string_credentials_js.benefit: Reading your code no longer gives access to your database.

db_tls_disabled_js.title: The database connection is not encrypted or not verified
db_tls_disabled_js.risk: This setting (ssl: false or tlsAllowInvalidCertificates: true) turns off encryption or the check of the server's certificate (its proof of identity). Someone on the network can then read the queries and passwords, or pose as the database.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Turn encryption on and keep the certificate check: ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: true, ca: fs.readFileSync("/etc/ssl/ca.crt").toString() } with pg, or tls: true with Mongoose.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

db_tls_disabled_js.benefit: Exchanges with the database stay private and reach the real server.

dependency_confusion.title: An internal package can be replaced by a public one with the same name
dependency_confusion.risk: Your project declares or loads a package whose name looks internal. If it is missing from the public package index, an attacker can publish one with that name, which the package manager may install instead.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Install your internal packages only from your private package index, never from a source that also searches the public index, and pin each version with its hash.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

dependency_confusion.benefit: Your project only installs your own internal packages.

different_kinds_comparison_bypass.title: A security check compares two values that both come from the visitor
different_kinds_comparison_bypass.risk: The code compares a value from the address (req.query or req.params) with one from the body, headers or cookies of the same request. The visitor writes both, so they only need to send the same value twice to pass the check.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Compare the value of the request with a value kept on the server, such as req.session.userId or a token stored in the session.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

different_kinds_comparison_bypass.benefit: The check relies on a value the visitor cannot choose.

disable_certificate_validation.title: The server's certificate is not checked on HTTPS connections
disable_certificate_validation.risk: rejectUnauthorized: false or NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED = "0" makes the program accept any certificate (the proof of identity of a server). Someone on the network can then pose as the server and read or change everything exchanged, passwords included.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove this setting; if the server uses a certificate you issued yourself, pass that certificate with the ca option: https.request({ hostname, ca: fs.readFileSync("ca.pem") }).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

disable_certificate_validation.benefit: The program only talks to the real server.

dom_pseudo_eval.title: Text is run as code by setTimeout or setInterval
dom_pseudo_eval.risk: When setTimeout() or setInterval() receives a text instead of a function, it runs that text as code, like eval(). Here the text is assembled with + or ${}, so if a part comes from a user, they can run their own code in the page.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Pass a function instead of a text: setTimeout(() => processData(userId), 1000).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

dom_pseudo_eval.benefit: No text can be run as code by your timers.

double_escaping.title: HTML escaping is partly undone by hand with replace()
double_escaping.risk: The code turns & back into & or < back into < with replace(), often right after escaping the text (turning < and > into harmless codes). Done by hand and only in part, this can bring back HTML that a visitor slipped into the text, which then runs in the page.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Escape the text once, with a single library, at the moment you insert it into the page, and remove the replace() calls that undo it.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

double_escaping.benefit: Text from visitors stays harmless text in the page.

electron_insecure_content.title: Electron lets HTTPS pages run scripts loaded over plain HTTP
electron_insecure_content.risk: The window option allowRunningInsecureContent: true lets a page loaded over HTTPS run scripts fetched over plain HTTP. Someone on the same network, such as public Wi-Fi, can replace those scripts and take control of the application window.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove allowRunningInsecureContent: true (or set it to false) and load every resource over HTTPS.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

electron_insecure_content.benefit: No one on the network can slip scripts into your application.

electron_node_integration.title: Electron gives web pages full access to the computer (nodeIntegration)
electron_node_integration.risk: With nodeIntegration: true, the pages shown in the window can use Node.js, which reads files and runs commands. If a page shows content from outside, an injected script gets the same power over the user's computer.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Isolate the pages from Node.js: 1) set nodeIntegration: false and contextIsolation: true; 2) expose only the few functions the page needs through contextBridge, in a preload script.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

electron_node_integration.benefit: A script in a page cannot reach the files or commands of the computer.

electron_web_security_disabled.title: Electron turns off the browser's protections (webSecurity: false)
electron_web_security_disabled.risk: With webSecurity: false, a page in the window can read data from any other site and load scripts over plain HTTP. A malicious or hijacked page can then reach other sites with the user's sessions and run code in the application.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove webSecurity: false so that the default protection applies; if you need data from another server, enable CORS (the rules for access between sites) on that server instead.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

electron_web_security_disabled.benefit: Each page in the application keeps the normal browser protections.

empty_password_config.title: A password is left empty in the configuration
empty_password_config.risk: A password is set to "", null or undefined. The database or service then accepts connections without a password, so anyone who can reach it can read or change its data.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Require a real password: 1) read it from an environment variable (process.env.DB_PASSWORD); 2) stop the program at startup when it is missing or empty; 3) set a password on the service itself.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

empty_password_config.benefit: Nobody can connect to your services without the password.

eval_template_literal.title: Code built from a template string is run with eval()
eval_template_literal.risk: The code passes a template string (text between backticks with ${...} inserts) to eval(), which runs it as JavaScript. If an inserted value comes from a user, they can write any code, and it runs with the rights of your program.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove eval(): read data with JSON.parse(), or pick the function to call from a fixed list, such as handlers[actionName].
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

eval_template_literal.benefit: No text can become code that runs in your program.

express_no_csrf.title: Express routes accept requests forged by other websites
express_no_csrf.risk: This file declares POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE routes but uses no CSRF protection (a check that a request really comes from your own pages). Another website can make a logged-in visitor's browser send such a request, and act in their name.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Protect these routes: 1) add a CSRF protection before them, such as lusca (app.use(lusca.csrf())) or csrf-csrf; 2) send its token (a secret value checked on each request) in your forms.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

express_no_csrf.benefit: Other websites can no longer act in the name of your visitors.

file_access_to_http.title: The content of a local file is sent in an HTTP request
file_access_to_http.risk: The code reads a file with fs.readFileSync() or require() and sends it at once with axios.post(), request.put() or a similar call. If the path or the target address can be influenced, server files such as passwords or keys go elsewhere.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Send only what the service needs: 1) choose the file from a fixed list, never from the request; 2) write the target address in your configuration.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

file_access_to_http.benefit: No file of your server can leave for an address you did not choose.

filesystem_race_condition.title: A file is checked, then used: it can change in between
filesystem_race_condition.risk: The code checks a file with fs.existsSync(), fs.access() or fs.stat(), then works on it in a second step. In between, another program can create, replace or redirect the file, so yours writes or reads where it did not intend.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Do the operation directly, without a separate check: 1) open or write with an option that refuses an existing file ({ flag: "wx" }); 2) handle the error it throws, such as EEXIST or ENOENT.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

filesystem_race_condition.benefit: No other program can slip a file in between the check and the use.

functionality_untrusted_domain.title: A file from another site is loaded without an integrity check
functionality_untrusted_domain.risk: A src or href attribute loads a file from another site without an integrity attribute (the fingerprint the file must match). If that site is hacked or changes the file, your visitors run its code in your pages.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Add a fingerprint to the tag: 1) compute it with openssl dgst -sha384 -binary file.js | openssl base64 -A; 2) add integrity="sha384-…" and crossorigin="anonymous" to the script or link tag.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

functionality_untrusted_domain.benefit: A file changed on the other site is refused instead of running in your pages.

functionality_untrusted_source.title: A script or style sheet is loaded over unencrypted HTTP
functionality_untrusted_source.risk: The page loads a script or a style sheet from an http:// address. Someone on the network, such as public Wi-Fi, can replace the file on the way and run their own code in your page.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Secure the loading: 1) use an https:// address; 2) add the integrity and crossorigin attributes so that the browser checks that the file has not changed.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

functionality_untrusted_source.benefit: The page only runs the exact files you chose.

graphql_batching_attack.title: A GraphQL server may accept many operations in one request
graphql_batching_attack.risk: This file starts a server (ApolloServer, graphqlHTTP or createServer) with no limit on batches (several operations sent in one request). One request can then try thousands of passwords, or overload the server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Limit what one request can do: 1) turn off batches (allowBatchedHttpRequests: false in Apollo Server 4) or cap their size; 2) limit the cost of each query and the number of requests per visitor.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

graphql_batching_attack.benefit: One request can no longer overload the server or test passwords in bulk.

hardcoded_data_as_code.title: Encoded data is run as code
hardcoded_data_as_code.risk: The code decodes hidden text (base64, hexadecimal, character codes or \x escapes) and runs it with eval() or Function(). Backdoors and malware use this trick to hide what they do from reviewers and security tools.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Decode the text to see what it does, then write that code in clear in your files; if you did not write it, remove it and check where it came from.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

hardcoded_data_as_code.benefit: All the code of your program can be read and reviewed.

host_header_poisoning.title: An email link is built from the Host header the visitor sends
host_header_poisoning.risk: The code builds the link of an email, such as a password reset link, from the Host header (the site name sent by the browser). A visitor can change that header, so an attacker can request a reset for a victim and make the victim's secret link point to the attacker's server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Build the links from an address set in your configuration, such as process.env.APP_BASE_URL, never from the Host header.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

host_header_poisoning.benefit: The links in your emails always point to your own site.

http_to_file_access.title: A downloaded file is saved without checking its content
http_to_file_access.risk: The program writes data received over the network straight to disk, without checking it. If the remote server is hacked or impersonated, it can place a modified file on your machine, for example a program or a configuration that is then used.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Check the file before writing it: 1) compute its fingerprint (a short code that changes as soon as one byte changes) with crypto.createHash("sha256").update(res.data).digest("hex"); 2) compare it with the value published by the source and stop if they differ; 3) write the file only to a fixed folder.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

http_to_file_access.benefit: Only files identical to the expected ones end up on your disk.

ide_config_exfil.title: The code writes into the settings of a code editor or AI assistant
ide_config_exfil.risk: The code writes a settings file in .claude/, .vscode/, .cursor/, .aider/ or .codeium/. Malicious packages do this so that their code runs again each time the editor starts, as in the TanStack/Mistral npm attack of May 2026.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Find out why this code writes there: a real setup script asks the user before changing editor settings; if you do not know where it comes from, remove the package and check the machine.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

ide_config_exfil.benefit: No package can hide code that starts again with your editor.

improper_code_sanitization.title: Code cleaned with replace() is still run with eval()
improper_code_sanitization.risk: The code removes a few characters with replace() and then runs the text with eval() or new Function(). Such cleaning always misses something, so whoever controls the text can still run any JavaScript in your program.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Stop running the text as code: read data with JSON.parse(), or map the allowed names to functions you wrote, such as ACTIONS[name].
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

improper_code_sanitization.benefit: No text from outside can run as code in your program.

incomplete_hostname_regexp.title: A site name is checked with a pattern whose dot accepts any character
incomplete_hostname_regexp.risk: A site name such as "example.com" is used as a search pattern (a regular expression), where a dot means any character. The check then also accepts names you did not intend, such as examplexcom or example.com.evil.net.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Write the pattern with escaped dots and fixed ends (^example\.com$), or compare the name directly with the expected domain.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

incomplete_hostname_regexp.benefit: Only the site names you intended pass the check.

incomplete_html_attribute_sanitization.title: A value is inserted into an HTML attribute without being checked
incomplete_html_attribute_sanitization.risk: The code builds HTML with a value inside an attribute such as href, src or onclick. A value like javascript:alert(1), or a quote that closes the attribute, lets an attacker run a script in the user's page.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Set the attribute with setAttribute() instead of building HTML, and accept for href or src only addresses that start with https:// or /.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

incomplete_html_attribute_sanitization.benefit: No value can add a script to your page through an attribute.

incomplete_multichar_sanitization.title: Dangerous tags are removed with a simple text replace
incomplete_multichar_sanitization.risk: Calling replace() with a text such as "<script>" or "javascript:" removes only the first exact match. An attacker gets past it with "<SCRIPT>", a second copy, or "<scr<script>ipt>", which becomes "<script>" once cleaned.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Stop removing pieces of text: escape the HTML (turn its special characters into harmless text) before display, for example with textContent, or clean it with DOMPurify.sanitize() if you must keep some HTML.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

incomplete_multichar_sanitization.benefit: No variant of a tag can get past the protection.

incomplete_sanitization.title: replace() with a text removes only the first occurrence
incomplete_sanitization.risk: replace("../", "") with a text as first argument removes only its first occurrence. A value such as "../../secret" still contains "../" afterwards, so the cleaning you rely on does not work.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Do not clean by removing pieces: 1) for a file name, keep only path.basename(value); 2) for HTML, put the text in element.textContent; 3) in other cases, use replaceAll() and check the result.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

incomplete_sanitization.benefit: No piece left behind can slip through your cleaning.

incomplete_url_scheme_check.title: A link check blocks javascript: but not the other dangerous prefixes
incomplete_url_scheme_check.risk: The code rejects addresses that start with javascript: but lets through data: and vbscript:, which can also run scripts. The test is also fooled by capitals, so JavaScript: gets past it.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Accept only the prefixes you need instead of blocking the bad ones: for example, keep the address only if /^https?:/i.test(url).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

incomplete_url_scheme_check.benefit: Only web links get through, however they are written.

incomplete_url_substring_sanitization.title: An address is checked with startsWith(), endsWith() or includes()
incomplete_url_substring_sanitization.risk: The code checks an address by searching a domain name in its text, such as url.startsWith("https://safe.com"). The address https://safe.com.attacker.com passes this check, so a redirect or a server request can go to the attacker's site.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Read the server name with new URL(url).hostname and compare it with a list of allowed names: ALLOWED.includes(hostname).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

incomplete_url_substring_sanitization.benefit: Only the servers on your list pass the check.

incorrect_suffix_check.title: The end of a text is checked with indexOf() instead of endsWith()
incorrect_suffix_check.risk: The code compares s.indexOf(suffix) with s.length - suffix.length to check how a text ends. When the text is one character shorter than the ending, both sides equal -1 and the check passes, letting a wrong name through. It also fails when the ending already appears earlier in the text.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Call endsWith() instead: return filename.endsWith(".png").
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

incorrect_suffix_check.benefit: The check of a file name or domain ending gives the right answer in every case.

indirect_command_injection.title: A system command is built by joining texts
indirect_command_injection.risk: This command passed to exec() or spawn() is built by joining texts with + or ${}. If one part comes from a user, a character such as ; or | lets them add their own command and run it on the server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Pass the program and its arguments separately, without a shell (the command interpreter): execFile("convert", [filename, "-resize", "800x", outputFile]) or spawn("convert", [filename, "-resize", "800x", outputFile]).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

indirect_command_injection.benefit: Text sent by a user stays a simple argument and can never become a command.

inline_event_handler.title: JavaScript is attached through an on… attribute such as onclick
inline_event_handler.risk: Code is attached with an attribute or property such as onclick or onerror, or with setAttribute("on…"). If its text comes from a visitor, it runs as code in your page. In HTML, such attributes also prevent a strict CSP (the rules that block unknown scripts) from protecting the page.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Attach code from your script files: 1) replace each on… attribute with element.addEventListener("click", handler); 2) never pass visitor text to setAttribute() for an attribute whose name starts with on.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

inline_event_handler.benefit: Visitor text can no longer run as code, and your CSP can block unknown scripts.

insecure_dependency_http.title: An address uses http:// or ftp://, without encryption
insecure_dependency_http.risk: The code or package.json contains an address starting with http:// or ftp://, so what it points to travels unencrypted. Someone on the network can read it or swap it, for example replace a dependency with malicious code that runs at npm install.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Replace http:// with https:// in the address, and for a dependency, better still, publish it to an npm registry and refer to it by name and version.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_dependency_http.benefit: Nobody on the network can read or replace what the address points to.

insecure_download.title: A file or script is downloaded over HTTP, without encryption
insecure_download.risk: The code points to a program, archive or script at an http:// address (a .exe, .sh or .zip file, or a fetch() or require() call). Someone on the network can replace it with malicious code, which then runs on your machine or on your users' machines.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Secure the download: 1) use an https:// address; 2) compare the SHA-256 fingerprint of the file with the one published by its author before running it.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_download.benefit: Nobody on the network can swap the file you download.

insecure_random_js.title: Math.random() makes values that can be guessed
insecure_random_js.risk: Math.random() is not built to be unpredictable: its next values can be guessed from earlier ones. If it makes a token, a reset code or a key, an attacker can guess it and take over the account.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use crypto.randomUUID() or crypto.getRandomValues() for any value that must stay secret, and keep Math.random() for games and visual effects.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_random_js.benefit: Nobody can guess your tokens and codes.

insecure_temp_file.title: A temporary file name can be known or taken in advance
insecure_temp_file.risk: The program uses a temporary file whose name another program can guess or claim before it is created. That program can then put a file or a link there, and make yours write where it chooses or read your data.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Create each temporary file and its random name in a single step, with your language's secure temporary-file function, and make it readable only by your account.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_temp_file.benefit: No other program can prepare or swap your temporary file.

insufficient_password_hash.title: A password is hashed with a fast function (MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256)
insufficient_password_hash.risk: MD5 and SHA are fast: a graphics card tries billions of passwords per second against a stolen hash (a one-way fingerprint of the password). If your database leaks, most passwords are found within hours.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Hash passwords with a function made to be slow, such as bcrypt: await bcrypt.hash(password, 12), checked with bcrypt.compare().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insufficient_password_hash.benefit: A stolen password database takes years, not hours, to crack.

javascript_uri.title: A javascript: address runs code when it is opened
javascript_uri.risk: An address starting with javascript: runs the code that follows it when a visitor clicks or the page loads it. If part of that text comes from a visitor, a hostile script runs in your page and can steal sessions or redirect users.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Separate the link from the code: 1) give it a real address, or use a <button> if it does not open a page; 2) run the code with element.addEventListener("click", handler).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

javascript_uri.benefit: No address in your page can run code.

jwt_missing_verification.title: Login tokens (JWT) are checked without a real secret key
jwt_missing_verification.risk: A JWT is a token (a signed code that proves who the user is). Here jwt.verify() gets no real key (false, null or undefined) or an empty list of algorithms, so a forged token can be accepted.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Always pass your real key and name the accepted algorithm: jwt.verify(token, process.env.JWT_SECRET, { algorithms: ["HS256"] }).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

jwt_missing_verification.benefit: Only tokens signed by your server are accepted.

jwt_weak_secret.title: Login tokens are signed with a short secret written in the code
jwt_weak_secret.risk: jwt.sign() signs the token (the proof of login given to the user) with a secret of fewer than 16 characters written in the code. An attacker can guess it by trying many values, then create valid tokens and log in as anyone.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Replace the secret: 1) generate a random one of at least 32 characters with crypto.randomBytes(32).toString("hex"); 2) read it from an environment variable: jwt.sign(data, process.env.JWT_SECRET).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

jwt_weak_secret.benefit: No one can forge a login token for your application.

loop_bound_injection.title: A loop runs as many times as the request asks
loop_bound_injection.risk: The number of turns of a for loop comes straight from the request. A visitor can send a huge number, such as 2147483647, and keep the server busy for a long time, which blocks it for every other user.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Convert the value to a number and cap it before the loop: const count = Math.min(parseInt(req.body.count, 10) || 0, MAX).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

loop_bound_injection.benefit: No request can make the loop run past the limit you set.

mass_assignment_js.title: The whole request body is used to create a record
mass_assignment_js.risk: The code passes req.body as it is to create() or to a model constructor. A visitor can add fields you did not plan, such as role or isAdmin, and give themselves rights.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Copy only the fields you allow: const { name, email } = req.body, then User.create({ name, email }).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

mass_assignment_js.benefit: Visitors can only fill in the fields you chose.

missing_auth_middleware.title: A sensitive route has no login check
missing_auth_middleware.risk: A route (a server address that runs an action) that cancels, deletes, runs or triggers something goes straight to its handler, with no login check. Anyone who can reach the server can call it without being logged in.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Add your login check between the path and the handler, such as router.post(path, requireAuth, handler), or apply it to the whole router with router.use(requireAuth).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

missing_auth_middleware.benefit: Only logged-in users can start these actions.

missing_pkce_oauth.title: OAuth login without PKCE: the authorization code can be stolen
missing_pkce_oauth.risk: With OAuth (login through another service), your app receives a one-time code, then exchanges it for access. Without PKCE (a secret your app creates for each login), a malicious app or extension that intercepts this code can use it to log in as the user.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Add PKCE to each login: 1) create a random code_verifier and send its SHA-256 fingerprint as code_challenge, with code_challenge_method=S256; 2) send the code_verifier when you exchange the code.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

missing_pkce_oauth.benefit: A stolen authorization code is useless without the secret of your app.

missing_rate_limit.title: A login or password route may accept unlimited attempts
missing_rate_limit.risk: This route (an address of your server, declared with app.post or router) handles a login, a password, a code or a token. No request limit is set for it or for the whole server. It answers every request, however many arrive, so someone can try thousands of passwords or codes until one works.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Limit the number of attempts per visitor: 1) install express-rate-limit; 2) create a limiter, const loginLimiter = rateLimit({ windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000, max: 5 }); 3) pass it to the route before its handler: app.post("/login", loginLimiter, loginHandler).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

missing_rate_limit.benefit: Nobody can try passwords or codes in bulk on your server.

missing_regexp_anchor.title: An address check can be fooled (^ and $ missing in the pattern)
missing_regexp_anchor.risk: This regular expression (a text pattern) checks a domain name such as example.com without ^ at the start and $ at the end. It then also accepts example.com.attacker.net, so the check lets through addresses it should refuse.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Add ^ at the start and $ at the end of the pattern: /^(www\.)?example\.com$/.test(host), or compare new URL(address).hostname with a list of allowed names.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

missing_regexp_anchor.benefit: Only the exact addresses you allow pass the check.

missing_x_frame_options.title: Other sites can show your pages inside a hidden frame
missing_x_frame_options.risk: This Express app never sends the X-Frame-Options header (an instruction that forbids showing the page inside another site). A malicious site can then show your page invisibly and trick a visitor into clicking a button on it, such as "Delete my account".

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Add Helmet, which sends this header: 1) install it with npm install helmet; 2) after const app = express(), add app.use(helmet()).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

missing_x_frame_options.benefit: No other site can show your pages to trick your visitors.

mongo_operator_injection.title: A MongoDB query uses an object sent by the visitor as is
mongo_operator_injection.risk: The code passes req.body, req.query or req.params straight to find(), findOne(), updateOne(), deleteOne() or aggregate(). A visitor can put MongoDB operators (special keys) such as {"$ne": null} in it, to log in without a password or reach other users' data.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Build the query yourself from the fields you expect, each converted to text: findOne({ email: String(req.body.email) }), or clean the input with express-mongo-sanitize.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

mongo_operator_injection.benefit: The visitor can only send values, not change the query.

npm_git_dependency.title: npm dependency pinned to a third-party Git commit
npm_git_dependency.risk: package.json declares a dependency pointing to a specific Git commit on a third-party host. This vector was used in the TanStack/Mistral npm supply-chain attack (May 2026) — an attacker can swap commits without triggering version bumps and bypass npm registry advisories. Untrusted host commits should not be installed.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Pin dependencies to versions published on the npm registry (e.g. ^1.169.5). If a Git source is unavoidable, vendor the audited code or host an internal fork rather than tracking an upstream commit hash directly.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

npm_git_dependency.benefit: Closes a documented npm supply-chain attack vector and ensures npm registry advisories cover all installed code.

npm_lifecycle_script.title: A package.json script runs on its own at install time
npm_lifecycle_script.risk: A preinstall, postinstall or preuninstall script runs on its own during npm install, on every developer machine and build server. If it comes from a hijacked package or an unknown author, it can steal secrets or install malware.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Read the script and keep it only if you know what it does: 1) remove any script that downloads and runs code (curl … | sh); 2) install with npm ci --ignore-scripts where scripts are not needed.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

npm_lifecycle_script.benefit: Installing your dependencies no longer runs unknown code.

overly_large_regex_range.title: Overly large regex character range
overly_large_regex_range.risk: A character class range like [A-z] or [a-Z] spans non-alphabetic ASCII characters (backslash, brackets, caret) between the upper and lower case ASCII ranges, matching unintended characters and potentially allowing filter bypass (CWE-020).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Write each range separately, such as [A-Za-z] instead of [A-z], so that the pattern only accepts the characters you meant.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

overly_large_regex_range.benefit: Ensures regex only matches intended characters, preventing filter bypass.

password_in_config_file.title: A password is written in clear in the code
password_in_config_file.risk: A "password" key holds a real password written in the file. Anyone who can read the project, or its history, gets it, and it stays in the history even after it is deleted.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove the password from the code: 1) read it from an environment variable (password: process.env.DB_PASSWORD); 2) change it, since the old one stays in the history.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

password_in_config_file.benefit: Reading the code is no longer enough to get your passwords.

private_file_exposure.title: Private folders are published on the website (node_modules, .git, .env…)
private_file_exposure.risk: express.static() here serves a folder that should stay private (node_modules, .git, .env, src, config or secrets). Anyone can then download your source code, its history or your passwords just by typing the right address.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Serve only a folder made for the public, such as public or dist: app.use(express.static(path.join(__dirname, "public"))).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

private_file_exposure.benefit: Visitors can download only the files meant for them.

prompt_injection_llm.title: Text from a visitor is sent to an AI model without precautions
prompt_injection_llm.risk: The text of the visitor is mixed with your instructions to the AI model (LLM). The visitor can then write instructions of their own, for example to make the model reveal hidden data or ignore your rules.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Put your instructions in the system message and the text of the visitor in a separate user message, limit its length, and give the model no data or action the visitor may not have.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

prompt_injection_llm.benefit: A visitor cannot make the model do more than they are allowed to.

prototype_pollution.title: An object is filled with keys that may include __proto__
prototype_pollution.risk: The code copies keys from one object to another with for...in, Object.assign() or __proto__. If the data comes from a visitor, a key named __proto__ changes the model shared by all objects (the prototype), which can bypass checks or crash the server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Skip the dangerous keys when you copy: 1) loop over Object.keys(source) instead of for...in; 2) ignore the keys __proto__, constructor and prototype; 3) for data from visitors, use a Map or an object created with Object.create(null).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

prototype_pollution.benefit: No visitor can change how all the objects of your program behave.

redis_eval_injection_js.title: A script run by Redis is built from user data
redis_eval_injection_js.risk: EVAL runs a Lua script (a small program) inside Redis, and here a value from the user is pasted into that script. An attacker can then add their own code and read or change any key in Redis.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Write the script as fixed text and pass the values separately, as KEYS or ARGV: client.eval("return redis.call('GET', KEYS[1])", 1, req.body.key).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

redis_eval_injection_js.benefit: User data can only be a value, not change the script.

regex_dos.title: A search pattern built from user input can block the server
regex_dos.risk: new RegExp() turns text sent by a user into a regular expression (a search pattern). A pattern written to be slow can keep the server busy for seconds or minutes, and no other visitor is served meanwhile.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Search for the text as plain text instead of a pattern: item.name.includes(String(req.query.search)); if you really need a pattern, escape its special characters first with the escape-string-regexp package.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

regex_dos.benefit: No text typed by a user can block your server.

regex_injection.title: A search pattern is taken from user data
regex_injection.risk: A value from the user is used as a regular expression (a text search pattern). An attacker can send a pattern that takes minutes to check and blocks the server, or one that matches everything and gets past a check.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Escape the value so that it is searched as plain text, with the escape function of your language, or let the user choose only among patterns you wrote.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

regex_injection.benefit: The user can only search for text, not write the pattern.

regex_redos_js.title: A search pattern built from user input can block the server
regex_redos_js.risk: new RegExp() turns text sent by a user into a regular expression (a search pattern). A pattern written to be slow can keep the server busy for seconds or minutes, and no other visitor is served meanwhile.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Search for the text as plain text instead of a pattern: item.name.includes(String(req.query.search)); if you really need a pattern, escape its special characters first with the escape-string-regexp package.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

regex_redos_js.benefit: No text typed by a user can block your server.

remote_property_injection.title: Properties sent by the visitor are copied into an object
remote_property_injection.risk: The code copies every key of the request into an object, with Object.assign() or a loop like obj[key] = value. A visitor can then overwrite fields such as isAdmin, or send a __proto__ key that changes how objects behave.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Copy only the keys you expect: keep those of a fixed list, such as ALLOWED_KEYS, and never copy __proto__, constructor or prototype.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

remote_property_injection.benefit: A visitor can only set the fields you allowed.

resource_exhaustion.title: A number sent by the visitor sets the size of an array or a loop
resource_exhaustion.risk: The code creates an array, or runs a loop, as many times as a number taken from the request (req.query, req.body…) says. A visitor who sends a huge number can fill the memory or keep the processor busy, and the service stops answering for everyone.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Clamp the number before using it, with a maximum you choose: const count = Math.min(parseInt(req.query.count, 10) || 0, MAX_ITEMS).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

resource_exhaustion.benefit: A visitor can no longer exhaust the server's memory or processor with one number.

samesite_none_cookie.title: SameSite=None cookie without Secure
samesite_none_cookie.risk: A cookie with SameSite: "none" but without the Secure attribute will be rejected by modern browsers, or if accepted, transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections — browsers require Secure when SameSite=None since Chrome 80, and non-Secure SameSite=None cookies enable CSRF (CWE-1275).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Add the Secure attribute next to SameSite=None, or use SameSite=Lax if the cookie is not needed on other sites.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

samesite_none_cookie.benefit: Ensures cross-site cookies are only transmitted over encrypted HTTPS connections.

second_order_command_injection.title: A system command is built from a value read from the database
second_order_command_injection.risk: The code passes a value read from a database or a cache (db, Model, redis…) to exec() or spawn(). If someone managed to store text in that place, even long ago, that text runs as a command on the server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Stop building the command from stored data: 1) write the command yourself and pass the value as a separate argument, with execFile("send-report", [name]); 2) check that the value has the expected format before the call.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

second_order_command_injection.benefit: Text stored in the database can no longer run commands on the server.

sensitive_get_query.title: A password or token is read from the address of a GET request
sensitive_get_query.risk: A GET route (app.get, router.get) reads a password, token or secret from req.query or req.params, so it travels in the address. Addresses end up in browser history and server logs, and are passed on to other sites, where other people can read them.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Receive secrets in the request body: 1) turn the route into app.post(); 2) read the value from req.body, over HTTPS.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

sensitive_get_query.benefit: Passwords and tokens no longer appear in addresses, histories or logs.

server_crash_unhandled.title: Malformed request data can crash the server
server_crash_unhandled.risk: This code reads request data with JSON.parse() or decodeURIComponent() without a try/catch block. A visitor who sends malformed text triggers an error that nothing catches, which can stop the Node.js server for all users.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Wrap the call in a try/catch block and answer with an error 400 when the data is invalid: try { data = JSON.parse(req.body.data); } catch { return res.status(400).end(); }
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

server_crash_unhandled.benefit: A malformed request gets an error message instead of stopping the server.

service_worker_hijack.title: A service worker is registered from an address that is not fixed
service_worker_hijack.risk: navigator.serviceWorker.register() installs a service worker (a script that intercepts all the requests of the pages it covers). Here its address is not written in full in the code. If it comes from the request, or a script can be injected into your site, an attacker keeps control of your pages, even after a fix.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Register only a script of your own site, at a fixed address, with the narrowest scope: navigator.serviceWorker.register("/static/sw.js", { scope: "/app/" }).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

service_worker_hijack.benefit: No outside script can take lasting control of your pages.

session_fixation.title: The session is not renewed at login
session_fixation.risk: The login code keeps the session identifier (the code the browser sends to be recognized) that the visitor had before logging in. An attacker who gave a victim a known identifier, for example through a link, can then act as the victim once logged in.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Call req.session.regenerate() as soon as the password is accepted, and save the user in the new session within the function you pass to it.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

session_fixation.benefit: An identifier known before login is worthless after it.

shell_injection_from_env.title: A shell command is built by gluing in an environment variable
shell_injection_from_env.risk: The code glues a value of process.env into a command that exec() or spawn() hands to the shell (the program that reads command lines). Whoever can set that variable, in the deployment settings or a parent process, can add their own commands.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Keep the variable out of the command text: 1) call execFile() with the program and its arguments in an array; 2) accept the variable only if its value is in a list you wrote.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

shell_injection_from_env.benefit: A changed environment variable can no longer add commands to yours.

sql_injection_raw_js.title: An SQL query is built by gluing a value into its text
sql_injection_raw_js.risk: The code passes to query() (pg, mysql2…) an SQL text built with + or with ${…} in a template string. A visitor who controls that value can change the query, to read, modify or delete any data in the database.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Put a placeholder in the query and pass the values apart: pool.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1", [userId]) with pg, or ? instead of $1 with mysql2.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

sql_injection_raw_js.benefit: Values sent by visitors can no longer change your SQL queries.

stored_xss.title: Data read from the database is inserted into the page as HTML
stored_xss.risk: The code puts a value read from the database into innerHTML, outerHTML, document.write() or insertAdjacentHTML(). If a user once saved a script in that data, it now runs in the browser of every visitor who opens the page.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Show the value with textContent instead of innerHTML. If you must show HTML, clean it first with DOMPurify.sanitize().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

stored_xss.benefit: A script saved in your data can no longer run in your visitors' browsers.

svelte_at_html.title: Svelte {@html} inserts a value into the page as HTML
svelte_at_html.risk: The {@html …} tag puts a value into the page as HTML, without escaping it (turning < and > into harmless text). If the value contains text from a user, a script hidden in it runs in the visitor's browser.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Write {value} instead of {@html value}, so Svelte shows it as text. If you must show HTML, clean it first with DOMPurify.sanitize().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

svelte_at_html.benefit: Text written by users is shown as text and cannot run in the browser.

taint_cmdi_js.title: Command injection: an attacker can run commands on the server
taint_cmdi_js.risk: Data sent by a visitor is placed in a system command run by your application. An attacker can then run their own commands on the server and take control of it.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Do not build the command as text: use execFile() with the program and an array of arguments instead of exec(), and accept only values planned in advance.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_cmdi_js.benefit: No one can run their own commands on your server.

taint_pathtraversal_js.title: Access to files outside the intended folder
taint_pathtraversal_js.risk: A file name sent by a visitor is used to open a file on the server. With « ../ » an attacker can read or write other files, such as your passwords or your configuration.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Check the path before opening the file: 1) compute the full path with path.resolve(), or keep only the file name with path.basename(); 2) reject it if it does not start with the allowed folder.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_pathtraversal_js.benefit: A visitor can only open the files you planned for.

taint_sqli_js.title: SQL injection: an attacker can read or change your database
taint_sqli_js.risk: Data sent by a visitor is inserted as it is into a database query. An attacker can then read, change or delete your data, including that of other users.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Pass the data to the query as a parameter instead of inserting it into its text: write the query with a placeholder (? or %s depending on your library) and give the value separately.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_sqli_js.benefit: Your data can no longer be read or changed through a crafted query.

taint_xss_js.title: Malicious code injected into your pages (XSS)
taint_xss_js.risk: Data sent by a visitor is shown as it is in a web page. An attacker can slip in a script that runs for other users and steals their session or their credentials.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Show the data with textContent instead of innerHTML, or let your framework escape it automatically: its special characters are then no longer read as code.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_xss_js.benefit: Your pages no longer run code supplied by a visitor.

tainted_format_string.title: Text from the request is used as a format template
tainted_format_string.risk: The first argument of util.format(), printf() or sprintf() is a template where codes such as %s or %j are replaced by the next values. Here that template comes from the request, so a visitor can add such codes and change or garble the text produced, for example in logs.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Write the template yourself and pass the text of the request as a value: util.format("%s", req.body.template).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

tainted_format_string.benefit: The text of the request is shown as is and cannot change the template.

telemetry_full_pii_by_default.title: Error reporting sends personal data (sendDefaultPii: true)
telemetry_full_pii_by_default.risk: With sendDefaultPii: true, the error-reporting tool (Sentry or similar) sends with each error the request headers, the cookies and the visitor's IP address. Login tokens and personal data thus go to an outside service without any review.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Set sendDefaultPii: false, and remove the Authorization and Cookie headers in beforeSend before each event leaves.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

telemetry_full_pii_by_default.benefit: Only the data needed to fix errors leaves for the outside service.

template_object_injection.title: The page template is taken straight from the request
template_object_injection.risk: The code gives render(), compile() or template() a value of the request (req.body, req.query…) as the template (a page model whose markers the engine fills in). These markers can run code on the server, so a visitor can read your settings or run commands.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Keep the template in your code and pass the visitor's data as variables: template.render("Hello, {{name}}!", { name: req.body.name }).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

template_object_injection.benefit: Visitors fill in your templates but can no longer write them.

token_exchange_full_scope_copy.title: A new token copies all the rights of the original key
token_exchange_full_scope_copy.risk: The code issues a new token (a digital access pass) with sign(), generateToken() or issueToken(). It copies there the scope (the list of allowed actions) of the original key or token. A token meant for one small task thus gets every right of that key, and so does whoever steals it.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Give the new token only the rights it needs: keep the actions that are both in the original scope and in a list you wrote for this exchange, for example intersectScopes(apiKey.scope, EXCHANGE_ALLOWED_SCOPES).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

token_exchange_full_scope_copy.benefit: A stolen token only opens what its task requires.

type_confusion_parameter.title: A request value is compared without checking that it is text
type_confusion_parameter.risk: A value of req.body, req.query or req.params is compared directly with a fixed text. A visitor can send a list or an object instead, for example ?role[]=admin: with == the list ["admin"] equals "admin", and a check with !== lets unexpected values through.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Check the type before comparing: accept the value only if typeof value === "string", or validate the whole request with a library such as Zod or express-validator.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

type_confusion_parameter.benefit: A list or an object sent by a visitor can no longer pass your checks.

unbounded_while_true_loop.title: A while (true) loop that reads data has no limit on its turns
unbounded_while_true_loop.risk: A while (true) loop reads or parses data (read(), exec(), a buffer, a stream…) without counting its turns. If a visitor sends data where the expected end never comes, the loop runs forever and the process stops answering.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Count the turns and stop at a maximum that does not depend on the data: while (iterations++ < MAX_ITERATIONS) { … }.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unbounded_while_true_loop.benefit: The loop always ends, whatever data it receives.

unrestricted_file_upload_js.title: Files are uploaded with no check on their type (Multer)
unrestricted_file_upload_js.risk: Multer receives the files that visitors send, but no fileFilter checks their type. A visitor can upload a script or a program, which may then run on the server or be served to other users.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Restrict what Multer accepts: 1) add a fileFilter that keeps only the types you expect (for example image/png or application/pdf); 2) set a size limit with limits.fileSize.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unrestricted_file_upload_js.benefit: Only the files you expect reach your server.

unsafe_code_construction.title: Code is built from text with new Function()
unsafe_code_construction.risk: new Function() turns a text into code, like eval(). Here the text is assembled while the program runs or comes from the request, so whoever controls part of it can run any code.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Never build code from text: write the function directly in your code, and to compute a formula typed by a user, use a dedicated library such as mathjs (math.evaluate(expr)).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unsafe_code_construction.benefit: No text sent by a user can run as code in your program.

unsafe_dynamic_method_access.title: A method is called by a name taken from the request
unsafe_dynamic_method_access.risk: The code calls obj[req.body.x](), so the visitor chooses which method of the object runs. They can reach methods you never meant to expose, including inherited ones such as constructor, and sometimes run their own code.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Accept only the method names of a list you wrote, and refuse the others before the call: if (!ALLOWED_ACTIONS.includes(action)) return res.status(400).end().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unsafe_dynamic_method_access.benefit: Visitors can only trigger the actions you chose.

unsafe_html_expansion.title: HTML tags are rewritten with a text pattern in replace()
unsafe_html_expansion.risk: The code rewrites HTML tags with replace() and a regular expression (a text search pattern), for example <tag/> into <tag>. Such a pattern does not read HTML like the browser does: a crafted text can come out as a working <script> tag.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Let the browser parse the HTML instead of a pattern: new DOMParser().parseFromString(html, "text/html"), then read doc.body.innerHTML.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unsafe_html_expansion.benefit: Tags are handled the way the browser sees them, so no script slips through the rewrite.

unsafe_reflection_from_deserialized_inpu.title: A class name taken from received data is used to create an object
unsafe_reflection_from_deserialized_inpu.risk: The code creates an object with new window[e.type](), where the class name comes from received data. Whoever controls that data chooses which constructor (function that creates an object) runs, among all those of the page, including dangerous ones.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
List the allowed classes in a fixed table and look the name up there: const ALLOWED = { Error, TypeError }; const Ctor = ALLOWED[e.type] || Error;
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unsafe_reflection_from_deserialized_inpu.benefit: Received data can only create objects of the classes you have chosen.

unsafe_require.title: require() loads a module whose name is computed
unsafe_require.risk: require() receives a variable instead of a fixed text, so the program loads whatever module that value names. If a visitor can influence it, they can make the server load and run another of its files.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Load only modules you chose: 1) write each name as a fixed text, in a table such as const handlers = { list: require("./list"), edit: require("./edit") }; 2) pick the module with handlers[action] and refuse unknown names.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unsafe_require.benefit: The program loads only the modules written in the code.

unvalidated_dynamic_method_call.title: A global function is called by a name taken from the request
unvalidated_dynamic_method_call.risk: The code calls window[…], global[…] or process[…] with a name from the request (req.body, req.query…). The visitor chooses any global function, such as eval or process.exit, to run their own code or stop the server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Map each allowed name to its function in an object you wrote, and refuse the others: const fn = ALLOWED[req.query.method]; if (!fn) return res.status(400).end().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unvalidated_dynamic_method_call.benefit: Visitors can no longer reach eval or any other global function.

url_host_parsing_via_string_split.title: The server name of an address is cut out with split() instead of URL
url_host_parsing_via_string_split.risk: The code finds the server name of an address with split('//')[1].split('/')[0]. Addresses with @, a backslash or odd encodings give another name here than in the browser or fetch(), which fools a check of allowed servers.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Read the server name with the URL class: const host = new URL(requestUrl).hostname.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

url_host_parsing_via_string_split.benefit: Your check sees the same server as the one actually contacted.

useless_regexp_escape.title: A backslash before a letter may do nothing in this pattern
useless_regexp_escape.risk: In a search pattern (a regular expression), a backslash before some letters does nothing: \h or \e just mean the letters h and e. The pattern then checks less than its author intended, and a check based on it can let wrong values through.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Check each backslash of the pattern: 1) remove it when the letter is meant as it is; 2) replace it with the right sequence when you meant a special one, such as \d for a digit or [ \t] for a space or a tab.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

useless_regexp_escape.benefit: The pattern matches exactly what you meant.

validate_before_canonicalize.title: A value is checked before being decoded or normalized
validate_before_canonicalize.risk: The code checks a value against an allowed or forbidden list, then decodes or converts it with decodeURIComponent(), .normalize() or .toLowerCase(). An encoded or upper-case value passes the check, then becomes the forbidden value once converted.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Convert first, check after: const resolved = decodeURIComponent(requestedPath).normalize(), then allowedPaths.includes(resolved), and use only resolved afterwards.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

validate_before_canonicalize.benefit: The check sees exactly the value that the code then uses.

vue_v_html.title: Vue v-html inserts a value into the page as HTML
vue_v_html.risk: The v-html attribute puts a value into the page as HTML, without escaping it (turning < and > into harmless text). If the value contains text from a user, a script hidden in it runs in the visitor's browser.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Show the value as text with {{ value }} or v-text. If you must show HTML, clean it first with DOMPurify.sanitize().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

vue_v_html.benefit: Text written by users is shown as text and cannot run in the browser.

websocket_no_validation.title: WebSocket messages are used without being checked
websocket_no_validation.risk: The ws.on("message") handler of a WebSocket (a connection that stays open between browser and server) uses the data without checking its form or size. Any client can send a huge message or unexpected fields, to crash the server or slip harmful values into the code.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Check each message before using it: 1) refuse messages above a size limit; 2) validate the content against a schema (a description of the expected fields) with zod, joi or ajv.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

websocket_no_validation.benefit: Only well-formed messages of a reasonable size reach your code.

window_open_noopener.title: window.open() lets the opened page control yours
window_open_noopener.risk: A page opened with window.open() gets a link back to yours, window.opener, unless "noopener" is given. If that page is hostile, it can send your tab to a fake copy of your site, for example a false login page.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Add "noopener,noreferrer" as the third argument: window.open(url, "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer").
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

window_open_noopener.benefit: The opened page can no longer touch your page.

xpath_injection.title: An XPath query is built from data of the request
xpath_injection.risk: The code passes a value of the request (req.body, req.query…) to an XPath function (a query language for XML documents) such as xpath.select(). A visitor can change the query to bypass a login check or read the whole document.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Write the query yourself with a variable, and pass the visitor's value apart: xpath.parse("/users/user[name = $name]").select({ node: doc, variables: { name: req.body.user } }).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

xpath_injection.benefit: Visitors' values are compared as data and can no longer change your XPath queries.

xss_exception_exposure.title: Error details are sent back to the visitor
xss_exception_exposure.risk: The code puts err.message or err.stack in the response with res.send(), res.json() or a similar call. Visitors then see file paths, library versions and internal names, which help them prepare an attack. With res.send(), a message that repeats visitor input can also run as HTML in the page.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Write the full error to your server logs with console.error(err), and send the visitor only a generic message: res.status(500).json({ error: "Internal server error" }).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

xss_exception_exposure.benefit: Visitors no longer see how your server is built inside.

xss_jquery_unsafe_plugin.title: jQuery .html() inserts a value from the page or the request as HTML
xss_jquery_unsafe_plugin.risk: The code gives $(…).html() a value read with .data(), .attr(), .val() or .text(), or taken from the request. This value is inserted as HTML, so a script hidden in it runs in the visitor's browser.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Call .text() instead of .html() to show the value. If you must show HTML, clean it first with DOMPurify.sanitize().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

xss_jquery_unsafe_plugin.benefit: The value is shown as text and cannot run in the browser.

xss_through_dom.title: A part of the page address is inserted into the page as HTML
xss_through_dom.risk: The code puts location.hash, location.search, document.URL, document.referrer or window.name into innerHTML or document.write(). Anyone can send a link that sets these values, and a script hidden in it runs in the browser of whoever opens the link.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Show the value with textContent instead of innerHTML. If you must show HTML, clean it first with DOMPurify.sanitize().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

xss_through_dom.benefit: A crafted link can no longer run a script in your page.

xss_unsafe_html_construction.title: Received text is inserted into the page as HTML
xss_unsafe_html_construction.risk: The code puts into innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML or document.write a text that comes from the request or is built with ${}. If that text contains a <script> tag or similar, the browser runs it, and an attacker can steal the visitor's session or act on their behalf.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Insert the text with textContent, which never interprets HTML: el.textContent = message; if you really need HTML, clean it first with DOMPurify.sanitize(html).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

xss_unsafe_html_construction.benefit: Text received from outside is shown as text and never runs as code.

db_error_exposed_php.title: An error message is sent as is to the user
db_error_exposed_php.risk: The response sent to the user contains the text of an error ($e->getMessage(), mysqli_error(), pg_last_error()). Database errors in particular reveal table names, columns or parts of queries, which help an attacker prepare a targeted attack.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Write the error to the server logs with error_log($e->getMessage()) and send the user a fixed message instead, such as {"error": "Internal error"}.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

db_error_exposed_php.benefit: Your error messages no longer reveal how your application and database are built.

hardcoded_connection_string_php.title: A database password is written in the code
hardcoded_connection_string_php.risk: The database connection (new PDO, new mysqli, mysqli_connect…) gets its password as text written in the code. Anyone who can read the code or its history can connect to your database.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove the password from the code: 1) read it from an environment variable with getenv('DB_PASSWORD'); 2) change the database password, since the old one stays in the history.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

hardcoded_connection_string_php.benefit: Reading the code no longer gives access to your database.

idor_missing_ownership_php.title: A record is fetched by its number without checking who owns it
