idor_missing_ownership_php.risk: The code loads a record with find() or findOrFail() and an identifier taken from the request, such as ?id=42, without checking that it belongs to the logged-in user. Changing the number is enough to see or change the data of other users.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Add the owner to the query: Order::where('id', $id)->where('user_id', auth()->id())->firstOrFail(), which answers "not found" when the record belongs to someone else.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

idor_missing_ownership_php.benefit: Each user only reaches their own data.

missing_authz_check_admin_controller.title: A sensitive action does not check that the user has the right to do it
missing_authz_check_admin_controller.risk: A controller method that deletes, updates, publishes, approves or exports data has no permission check nearby, such as $this->authorize() or Gate::. Any logged-in user who reaches it can then do it, whatever their role.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Check the right at the start of the method, with $this->authorize('reorder', GlobalSet::class) and a policy (a class that says who may do what), or with Gate::allows().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

missing_authz_check_admin_controller.benefit: Only users with the right role can run sensitive actions.

naive_domain_suffix_match_php.title: A domain is checked only by its end, so fake domains pass
naive_domain_suffix_match_php.risk: The code checks $host or $domain with str_ends_with(), strpos() or substr(), as plain text. The name evil-example.com ends with example.com without belonging to it, so an attacker's domain can pass the check and receive your cookies or your trust.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Accept the host only if it equals the domain or ends with a dot followed by the domain: $host === $domain || str_ends_with($host, '.' . $domain), and refuse IP addresses with filter_var($host, FILTER_VALIDATE_IP).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

naive_domain_suffix_match_php.benefit: Only your real domain and its subdomains pass the check.

oauth_account_link_without_email_verific.title: An account is linked through OAuth without checking the email was verified
oauth_account_link_without_email_verific.risk: The code finds or creates a local account from the email returned by an OAuth provider (a sign-in service such as Google or GitHub). It never checks that the provider verified that email. An attacker who registers your user's address at a lax provider can then sign in to that user's account.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Link or create the account only when the provider's answer says email_verified is true, and refuse the sign-in otherwise, for example with abort(403).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

oauth_account_link_without_email_verific.benefit: Nobody can take over an account with an email address they do not own.

password_reset_missing_token_binding_php.title: A password is reset without checking a reset token
password_reset_missing_token_binding_php.risk: This reset code changes a password with ->update(['password' => …]), with no check of a reset token (the single-use secret code sent by email) nearby. If the account is picked from an ID or an email in the request, anyone can change another user's password and take over the account.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Find the account from the reset token only: 1) look up the token's fingerprint in your reset table; 2) reject it when it is older than an hour or already used; 3) change the password of the account tied to it, then delete the token. With Laravel, Password::reset() does all three steps.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

password_reset_missing_token_binding_php.benefit: Only the person who received the reset email can change the password.

quadratic_uniqueness_check_in_loop.title: A loop searches a whole list with in_array() at each turn
quadratic_uniqueness_check_in_loop.risk: Inside a foreach loop, in_array() or array_search() reads the whole list to know if a value is already in it. With 10,000 items, that means millions of comparisons, and a large input can block the server for a long time.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Keep the values already seen as keys of an array and test them with isset($seen[$value]), which answers at once whatever the size of the list.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

quadratic_uniqueness_check_in_loop.benefit: The loop stays fast even when the list grows large.

sensitive_data_in_redirect.title: A redirect copies an address from the request as it is
sensitive_data_in_redirect.risk: The code sends header('Location: ' . $_GET[…]) with a value from the request, unchecked. The visitor can be sent to any site, and the address can carry tokens or session numbers that the target site then sees.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Keep only the path of the address with parse_url($target, PHP_URL_PATH), which drops the host and the parameters, and use "/" when it is empty or starts with //.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

sensitive_data_in_redirect.benefit: Redirects stay on your site and carry no sensitive data.

sensitive_field_exposed_response.title: A whole user record is sent in a JSON response
sensitive_field_exposed_response.risk: json_encode() or response()->json() receives a whole $user, $account or $customer object, with all its fields. The response can then contain the stored password fingerprint, access tokens or other secrets, and any field added later is sent too.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Send only the fields you choose, for example response()->json($user->only(['id', 'name', 'email'])), or list the secret fields in the $hidden property of the Eloquent model (the class tied to the database table).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

sensitive_field_exposed_response.benefit: Your responses contain only the data you chose to share.

stored_procedure_dynamic_php.title: A stored procedure call (CALL, EXEC) is built by pasting text together
stored_procedure_dynamic_php.risk: A text with CALL or EXEC, which runs a stored procedure (a program saved in the database), is joined with a PHP variable using the . operator. If that variable comes from a user, that user can add their own SQL, for example to read or delete all data.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Write the call with a placeholder and pass the value separately: $stmt = $pdo->prepare('CALL GetUser(:id)'), then $stmt->execute(['id' => $userId]).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

stored_procedure_dynamic_php.benefit: A value from a user can no longer change your queries.

taint_cmdi_php.title: Command injection: an attacker can run commands on the server
taint_cmdi_php.risk: Data sent by a visitor is placed in a system command run by your application. An attacker can then run their own commands on the server and take control of it.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Do not build the command from the raw data: protect each argument with escapeshellarg(), and accept only values planned in advance.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_cmdi_php.benefit: No one can run their own commands on your server.

taint_open_redirect_php.title: Open redirect: a link to your site can lead visitors to a fake site
taint_open_redirect_php.risk: Your site redirects the visitor, with header('Location: …') or wp_redirect(), to an address taken from the request, such as ?next=. An attacker can send a link that starts with your real address but leads to a fake site, for example to steal passwords.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Only redirect to pages of your own site: check with parse_url() that the requested address has no host other than yours, or that it is a path of your site (it starts with / but not with //), and use "/" otherwise.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_open_redirect_php.benefit: Links to your site can no longer be used to send visitors elsewhere.

taint_pathtraversal_php.title: Access to files outside the intended folder
taint_pathtraversal_php.risk: A file name sent by a visitor is used to open a file on the server. With « ../ » an attacker can read or write other files, such as your passwords or your configuration.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Check the path before opening the file: 1) compute the full path with realpath(), or keep only the file name with basename(); 2) reject it if it does not start with the allowed folder.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_pathtraversal_php.benefit: A visitor can only open the files you planned for.

taint_sqli_php.title: SQL injection: an attacker can read or change your database
taint_sqli_php.risk: Data sent by a visitor is inserted as it is into a database query. An attacker can then read, change or delete your data, including that of other users.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Pass the data to the query as a parameter instead of inserting it into its text: write the query with a placeholder (? or %s depending on your library) and give the value separately.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_sqli_php.benefit: Your data can no longer be read or changed through a crafted query.

taint_xss_php.title: Malicious code injected into your pages (XSS)
taint_xss_php.risk: Data sent by a visitor is shown as it is in a web page. An attacker can slip in a script that runs for other users and steals their session or their credentials.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Encode the data before showing it, with htmlspecialchars($value, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8'): its special characters are then no longer read as code.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_xss_php.benefit: Your pages no longer run code supplied by a visitor.

unbounded_decompression.title: Compressed data is unpacked with no size limit
unbounded_decompression.risk: gzinflate(), gzuncompress(), gzdecode(), zlib_decode() or bzdecompress() unpacks data with no limit on the result. A file of a few kilobytes can grow to several gigabytes, fill the memory and stop the server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Limit the size of the result: 1) pass the maximum as the second argument, for example gzinflate($data, 10 * 1024 * 1024), and reject the data when the call returns false; 2) for bzdecompress(), which has no such argument, refuse inputs above a fixed size checked with strlen().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unbounded_decompression.benefit: A small compressed file can no longer fill the server's memory.

unrestricted_file_upload_php.title: An uploaded file is saved without checking its type
unrestricted_file_upload_php.risk: move_uploaded_file() saves a file sent by a visitor, and nothing in this source file checks its extension or content. An attacker can send a .php script, then open it in the browser to run their code on your server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Check each file before saving it: 1) accept only the expected extensions, read with pathinfo($name, PATHINFO_EXTENSION) and compared with a fixed list; 2) check the real content with finfo_file(); 3) save it under a random name, for example bin2hex(random_bytes(16)); 4) store it outside the folders the site serves.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unrestricted_file_upload_php.benefit: Only the files you expect reach your server, and none of them can be run.

weak_password_hash_php.title: A password is hashed with a fast function (md5, sha1, sha256)
weak_password_hash_php.risk: md5, sha1 and sha256 compute a password's hash (the fingerprint stored instead of the password) in a fraction of a second. If your database leaks, an attacker can try billions of guesses per second and find most passwords.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Store passwords with password_hash(): 1) write password_hash($password, PASSWORD_DEFAULT) when the password is saved; 2) check a login with password_verify($input, $hash).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

weak_password_hash_php.benefit: A stolen password database becomes very slow and costly to crack.

authenticated_action_missing_authz.title: Authenticated action without authorization check
authenticated_action_missing_authz.risk: A view is protected by @login_required (authentication) but performs a sensitive administrative action with no permission check (authorization). Any authenticated user — not just staff — can trigger it. This is Missing Authorization (CWE-862): being logged in is not the same as being allowed.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Add an explicit permission check (user.has_perm(...), @staff_member_required, or a DRF permission class) in addition to @login_required for any administrative action.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

authenticated_action_missing_authz.benefit: Ensures administrative actions are restricted to users who actually hold the required role, not merely any logged-in user.

base64_credentials.title: A value is only hidden with base64, which anyone can decode
base64_credentials.risk: This text written in the code is encoded in base64 (a way to write data with plain letters), which is not encryption. Anyone who reads the code gets the original value back in one command, such as a password.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Remove the value from the code if it is a secret: 1) read it from an environment variable (os.environ["API_KEY"]) or from your secret manager; 2) replace it with a new value, since the old one stays in the history.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

base64_credentials.benefit: Reading your code no longer reveals your secrets.

cache_key_missing_user_scope.title: A cached answer is shared by all users
cache_key_missing_user_scope.risk: The function result is cached (kept in memory to answer faster) under a key that does not depend on the user. The first user's private data is then served to every user who calls it next.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Put the user's identifier in the cache key, for example with key_builder=lambda user: f"all_models:{user.id}".
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cache_key_missing_user_scope.benefit: Each user only gets the cached answers computed for them.

cache_poisoning.title: An unchecked proxy header can poison the cache for every visitor
cache_poisoning.risk: The code uses a header such as X-Forwarded-Host, which any visitor can set, to build addresses. If a cache (a copy of pages kept to serve them faster) stores that answer, every visitor then gets links to the attacker's site.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Accept the header only if its value is in your list of known hosts (ALLOWED_HOSTS), and build addresses from your own configuration otherwise.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cache_poisoning.benefit: No visitor can change the pages the cache serves to others.

case_sensitive_blocklist_bypass.title: An allow or block list treats upper and lower case as different
case_sensitive_blocklist_bypass.risk: The value is compared with the list exactly as written, so "Admin" and "admin" count as different. An attacker gets a blocked name accepted just by changing a letter to upper case.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Convert both sides to lower case before comparing: if name.lower() in {b.lower() for b in BLOCKLIST}.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

case_sensitive_blocklist_bypass.benefit: Changing the case of a letter no longer gets past the list.

cookie_injection.title: A cookie is set from a value sent by the visitor
cookie_injection.risk: The cookie value comes straight from the request. With a link that holds a semicolon or a line break, an attacker can add other cookies or settings to a victim's browser, such as a session they control.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Check the value before storing it: accept it only if it holds nothing but the characters you expect, re.fullmatch(r"[\w.-]+", name), and answer with an error otherwise.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cookie_injection.benefit: The cookie only ever holds the kind of value you expect.

cors_wildcard_origin.title: Any website can read this API's answers in a visitor's browser
cors_wildcard_origin.risk: The API accepts requests from every website (allow_origins=["*"], the CORS setting). A page on any site can then call it from a visitor's browser and read the answer, including the visitor's own data.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
List only the sites allowed to call the API (allow_origins=["https://app.example.com"]), and never combine "*" with allow_credentials=True.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cors_wildcard_origin.benefit: Only your own sites can read the API's answers in a visitor's browser.

csrf_missing_flask.title: A Flask action can be triggered from another website
csrf_missing_flask.risk: These Flask routes change data (POST, PUT, DELETE) without checking that the request comes from your own pages (CSRF protection). A page on another site can make a logged-in visitor's browser send it, for example to transfer money.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Turn on the protection of Flask-WTF with CSRFProtect(app): every form then carries a secret token that other sites cannot know. For an API used without cookies, authenticate each request with a token sent in a header.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

csrf_missing_flask.benefit: Another website can no longer act in the name of your logged-in visitors.

db_connection_string_credentials.title: A database address with its password is written in the code
db_connection_string_credentials.risk: This database address contains a user name and a password (user:password@host). Anyone who can read the code or its history, now or later, can connect to the database with it.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Remove the address from the code: 1) read it from an environment variable (os.environ["DATABASE_URL"]) or from your secret manager; 2) change the database password, since the old one stays in the history.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

db_connection_string_credentials.benefit: Reading your code no longer gives access to your database.

db_error_exposed_python.title: An error message is sent as is to the user
db_error_exposed_python.risk: The response sent to the user contains the text of an error (str(e)). Database errors in particular reveal table names, columns or parts of queries, which help an attacker prepare a targeted attack.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Write the error to the server logs with logger.exception("...") and send the user a fixed message instead, such as {"error": "Internal error"}.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

db_error_exposed_python.benefit: Your error messages no longer reveal how your application and database are built.

db_superuser_connection_python.title: The application connects to its database with an administrator account
db_superuser_connection_python.risk: The database account used here (root, sa, admin, postgres…) has every right on the database. If an attacker takes control of the application, they can read, change or delete all data, not only the application's own.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Create a database account for the application with only the rights it needs (for example SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE on its own tables), and connect with that account.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

db_superuser_connection_python.benefit: An attacker who takes over the application only reaches what its own account allows.

db_tls_disabled_python.title: The connection to the database is not encrypted
db_tls_disabled_python.risk: Encryption (TLS) is turned off for this database connection, or the certificate of the server is not checked. Someone on the network can then read the queries, the results and the password, or pose as the database.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Turn on TLS and check the certificate: sslmode="verify-full" with PostgreSQL, tls=True with MongoDB, and never ssl=False or CERT_NONE.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

db_tls_disabled_python.benefit: Data exchanged with the database stays private and comes from the real server.

django_mark_safe_xss.title: mark_safe() shows HTML without protection: a script can be injected
django_mark_safe_xss.risk: mark_safe() tells Django that a text is safe HTML, to be shown as is. If the text contains data from a user, they can insert a script that runs in other visitors' browsers and steals their session.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Build the HTML with format_html("

{}

", value), which protects the inserted values, and keep mark_safe() only for fixed text written by you.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

django_mark_safe_xss.benefit: User data shows as text and can no longer run as a script.

ecb_cipher_mode.title: Data is encrypted in ECB mode, which leaves patterns visible
ecb_cipher_mode.risk: The ECB mode encrypts each block of 16 bytes on its own, so two identical blocks give the same result. An attacker sees which parts of the data repeat, and can sometimes swap blocks without the key.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use the GCM mode with a new random nonce (a value used only once) for each message: AES.new(key, AES.MODE_GCM, nonce=os.urandom(12)).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

ecb_cipher_mode.benefit: Encrypted data no longer shows its patterns, and any change to it is detected.

elasticsearch_query_injection.title: An Elasticsearch search is taken whole from the request
elasticsearch_query_injection.risk: The body of the Elasticsearch search comes straight from the request. The visitor can then write any search: read documents they should not see, skip filters, or send a search heavy enough to block the server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Write the search yourself and only insert checked values from the request into it: es.search(body={"query": {"match": {"title": term[:100]}}}).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

elasticsearch_query_injection.benefit: The visitor can only fill in values to look for, not write the search.

hardcoded_iv_nonce.title: The starting value of an encryption (IV) is fixed in the code
hardcoded_iv_nonce.risk: An IV or nonce is a value that must change at each encryption. Here it is always the same, so the same message always gives the same encrypted result, and with some modes (GCM, CTR) messages can be read without the key.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Generate a new random value for each encryption, with os.urandom(16) or secrets.token_bytes(16), and store it next to the encrypted data.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

hardcoded_iv_nonce.benefit: Two encryptions of the same message no longer look alike.

hardcoded_tmp_path.title: A temporary file has a fixed name in /tmp
hardcoded_tmp_path.risk: The folder /tmp is shared by every program on the machine. Another program can create a file of the same name first, or a link to another file, and make yours read its data or overwrite another file.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Let Python choose a new, unique name: tempfile.mkstemp() for a file, tempfile.mkdtemp() for a folder, or tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

hardcoded_tmp_path.benefit: No other program can prepare or swap your temporary file.

host_allowlist_substring_bypass.title: A host name is only checked on its end, and a fake name gets through
host_allowlist_substring_bypass.risk: The code checks a host name with endswith() or startswith() on the raw text. A name such as "evil-internal.corp" ends with "internal.corp" without being part of it, so an attacker gets past the list of allowed or blocked names.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Extract the host with urllib.parse.urlparse(), then compare it exactly with the allowed name, or check that it ends with "." followed by that name.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

host_allowlist_substring_bypass.benefit: Only the names you allow, and their real subdomains, get through.

http_smuggling.title: HTTP request smuggling
http_smuggling.risk: Inconsistent Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding headers enable request smuggling attacks.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Normalize headers server-side and reject ambiguous requests.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

http_smuggling.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security (CWE-444, OWASP A04).

incomplete_url_sanitization.title: A web address is checked by its start or end only
incomplete_url_sanitization.risk: The code accepts an address because it starts or ends with a domain name. An address such as https://safe.com.attacker.net passes the check for https://safe.com, so the visitor is sent, or the server connects, to a site the attacker owns.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Read the host part of the address with urlparse(url).netloc (from urllib.parse) and compare it exactly with your list of allowed hosts (ALLOWED_HOSTS).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

incomplete_url_sanitization.benefit: Only the sites you listed pass the check.

insecure_cipher.title: Data is encrypted with an old algorithm known to be broken
insecure_cipher.risk: DES, 3DES, RC2, RC4, Blowfish and similar algorithms are too weak today. Encrypted data can be read without the key, with ordinary computers or known attacks.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use AES in GCM mode (AES.new(key, AES.MODE_GCM)) or ChaCha20-Poly1305, with a key of 256 bits.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_cipher.benefit: Encrypted data can only be read with the key.

insecure_cookie_no_secure.title: A cookie is set with secure=False
insecure_cookie_no_secure.risk: With secure=False, the browser also sends the cookie over plain HTTP. Anyone on the same network, such as public Wi-Fi, can read it and use the session it holds.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Replace secure=False with secure=True: response.set_cookie("token", value, secure=True, httponly=True).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_cookie_no_secure.benefit: The cookie only travels over encrypted connections.

insecure_db_deserialization_python.title: Data read from the database is loaded with pickle, which can run code
insecure_db_deserialization_python.risk: pickle.loads() rebuilds Python objects and can run code hidden in the data. Anyone who can change this column of the database, for example through an SQL injection, can then run commands on the server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Store the data as JSON and read it with json.loads(); if you must keep pickle, sign each value with hmac and check the signature before loading it.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_db_deserialization_python.benefit: Reading the database can no longer run code on your server.

insecure_ssl_version.title: A secure connection uses an old version or skips its checks
insecure_ssl_version.risk: The code asks for SSLv2, SSLv3, TLS 1.0 or 1.1, which are known to be broken, or for a context that skips certificate checks (ssl._create_unverified_context). Someone on the network can then read or change the exchanged data.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use ssl.create_default_context(), which checks certificates, and set ctx.minimum_version = ssl.TLSVersion.TLSv1_2.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_ssl_version.benefit: Exchanged data stays private and cannot be changed on the way.

jinja2_autoescape_false.title: Jinja2 pages are built without protecting the HTML
jinja2_autoescape_false.risk: With autoescape=False, Jinja2 inserts values in the page without escaping them (turning < and > into harmless text). A value from a user can then add a script to the page, which runs in the browser of every visitor who sees it.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Turn on escaping: jinja2.Environment(autoescape=select_autoescape(["html", "xml"])), and keep |safe for text you wrote yourself.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

jinja2_autoescape_false.benefit: A value from a user is shown as text and can no longer add a script.

llm_output_to_sink.title: An answer from an AI model is used in a command or query without checks
llm_output_to_sink.risk: The text returned by an AI model (LLM) goes into a dangerous place: an SQL query, a shell command, a file path or eval. Whoever can influence the model, for example through a document it reads, can then run commands or read data.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Treat the answer like data from a visitor: check it against what you expect (a list of allowed values, a strict format), pass it as a parameter of the query, and never give it to eval or a shell.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

llm_output_to_sink.benefit: Whatever the model answers, it cannot run commands or change your queries.

mass_assignment_python.title: Every field sent in the request is copied into an object
mass_assignment_python.risk: The code unpacks the whole request into an object, as in User(**request.json). A visitor only has to add a field such as is_admin, role or balance to the request to set it.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Copy only the fields you allow: allowed = ("name", "email", "bio"), then User(**{k: request.json[k] for k in allowed if k in request.json}), or go through a Django form that lists its fields.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

mass_assignment_python.benefit: Visitors can only change the fields you chose.

missing_session_timeout.title: Sessions stay valid for days or months
missing_session_timeout.risk: The session lifetime is set to more than a day, up to a year or more. A session cookie stolen or left on a shared computer keeps working all that time.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Shorten sessions to what your users need, for example one hour: SESSION_COOKIE_AGE = 3600 with Django, PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME = timedelta(hours=1) with Flask.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

missing_session_timeout.benefit: A stolen or forgotten session soon stops working.

missing_timeout.title: Missing request timeout
missing_timeout.risk: HTTP requests without timeout can hang indefinitely, causing resource exhaustion.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Add timeout parameter to all HTTP requests: requests.get(url, timeout=30).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

missing_timeout.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security (CWE-400, OWASP A06).

nosql_operator_injection_python.title: A MongoDB query uses $where or operators built from user data
nosql_operator_injection_python.risk: The $where operator runs JavaScript on the database server, and operators such as $regex or $gt change what a query matches. Built from user data, they let an attacker read other records, skip a password check or overload the server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Compare fields with plain values only ({"username": username}, after checking that it is a string), never use $where with user data, and turn $where off on the server if you do not need it.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

nosql_operator_injection_python.benefit: User data is only a value to look for and can no longer change the query.

os_system_injection.title: A command is run through the system shell (os.system, os.popen)
os_system_injection.risk: os.system() and os.popen() hand a whole line of text to the shell (the program that runs system commands). If part of it comes from a user, a character such as ; lets them add their own command and take control of the server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Run the command with subprocess.run() and a list of arguments, without the shell: write subprocess.run(["ping", "-c", "1", host]) instead of os.system(f"ping {host}").
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

os_system_injection.benefit: No user data can turn into a command on your server.

pam_auth_bypass.title: A PAM login accepts expired or locked accounts
pam_auth_bypass.risk: pam.authenticate() only checks the password (PAM is the login system of Linux). Without a call to acct_mgmt() afterwards, an expired, locked or disabled account can still log in.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Call acct_mgmt() after a successful authenticate(), and refuse the login if it fails: if p.authenticate(user, password) and p.acct_mgmt(user).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

pam_auth_bypass.benefit: Only active accounts can log in.

paramiko_no_host_key.title: SSH connections accept any server without checking its identity
paramiko_no_host_key.risk: With AutoAddPolicy or WarningPolicy, paramiko accepts the key of any server it has never seen. Someone on the network can pose as the server and read the password and the commands.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Load the known keys (client.load_system_host_keys()) and refuse unknown servers with client.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.RejectPolicy()).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

paramiko_no_host_key.benefit: Your program only talks to the real server.

parser_without_try.title: Parser without error handling
parser_without_try.risk: Unhandled parsing exceptions crash the application and may leak internal details.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Wrap parsing calls in try/except with appropriate error handling.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

parser_without_try.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

partial_ssrf.title: The server fetches an address partly chosen by the user
partial_ssrf.risk: Your server builds the address of a web request by adding a value, which may come from the user, to a fixed start (BASE_URL + path). By changing that part, an attacker can reach other pages or internal services that should stay private.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Check the added part before building the address: accept only the expected characters (for example with re.fullmatch(r"[a-zA-Z0-9/_-]+", path)) and refuse the values that contain .., //, @ or a prefix such as http:.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

partial_ssrf.benefit: Your server only reaches the pages you intended.

password_reversible_storage_python.title: Passwords are stored in a form that can be turned back into the original
password_reversible_storage_python.risk: The password is encoded or encrypted (base64, Fernet, AES), so it can be turned back into the original. Whoever steals the database, and the key if there is one, gets the real password of every user.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Store a password hash instead (a one-way fingerprint that cannot be turned back), made with bcrypt, Argon2id or scrypt: bcrypt.hashpw(password.encode(), bcrypt.gensalt()).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

password_reversible_storage_python.benefit: A stolen database no longer reveals the passwords of your users.

path_traversal_os_join.title: A file path built from user data can leave its folder
path_traversal_os_join.risk: A file path is built with os.path.join from data the user sends. With a name such as ../../etc/passwd, an attacker can read or overwrite files outside the intended folder, such as configuration files or passwords.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Check the final path before using it: 1) compute it with os.path.realpath(os.path.join(FOLDER, name)); 2) refuse the request if the result does not start with the real path of FOLDER (os.path.realpath(FOLDER)).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

path_traversal_os_join.benefit: Users can only reach the files of the folder you allow.

permissive_file_permissions.title: A file is made readable and writable by every user of the machine
permissive_file_permissions.risk: os.chmod gives this file the rights 777 or 766: every account on the machine can read it, and often change it. Another program or user can then read secrets in it or replace its content.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Give the file only the rights it needs: 0o600 (only its owner reads and writes it) for a file that holds secrets, 0o644 (others can only read it) for a public file.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

permissive_file_permissions.benefit: Other accounts on the machine can no longer read or change this file.

pii_in_url.title: Personal data (email, phone…) is placed in a web address
pii_in_url.risk: Web addresses are recorded in many places: server and proxy logs, browser history, analytics tools. An email or a phone number put in an address ends up in all of them, which breaks data-protection rules such as the GDPR.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Identify the person with an identifier that means nothing in the address (/users/<uuid:user_id>), and send personal data in the body of a POST request.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

pii_in_url.benefit: Personal data no longer ends up in logs and browser histories.

privileged_action_missing_role_check.title: A sensitive action does not check the user's rights
privileged_action_missing_role_check.risk: This function performs a sensitive action (delete, revoke, promote, shut down…) without checking nearby that the user has the right to do it. Any logged-in user, not only an administrator, may then trigger it.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Check the user's right at the start of the function, for example with if not user.has_permission("user:delete"): abort(403), or with the role check of your web library (a decorator such as @admin_required).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

privileged_action_missing_role_check.benefit: Only the people you allow can perform this action.

race_condition_financial.title: A balance or stock is changed without a lock, so two requests can collide
race_condition_financial.risk: The code reads a value such as a balance, then writes the new value, with nothing that stops two requests from doing it at the same time. Sent together, two payments can both pass with money for only one, or a stock can drop below zero.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Make the change in one step in the database: lock the row with select_for_update() inside transaction.atomic(), or write balance = F("balance") - amount.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

race_condition_financial.benefit: Requests sent at the same time can no longer spend the same money twice.

redis_eval_injection_python.title: A script run by Redis is built from user data
redis_eval_injection_python.risk: EVAL runs a Lua script (a small program) inside Redis, and here a value from the user is pasted into that script. An attacker can then add their own code and read or change any key in Redis.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Write the script as fixed text and pass the values separately, as KEYS or ARGV: r.eval("return redis.call('GET', KEYS[1])", 1, user_key).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

redis_eval_injection_python.benefit: User data can only be a value, not change the script.

redos_nested_quantifier.title: A search pattern can take so long that it blocks the program
redos_nested_quantifier.risk: This search pattern (a regular expression), compiled with re.compile, contains a repetition inside another one, such as (a+)+. On some well-chosen texts, checking it takes minutes instead of microseconds, and whoever sends such a text blocks the program.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove the repetition nested in another one: write a+b instead of (a+)+b, or use the re2 library, which checks every pattern in a time proportional to the text.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

redos_nested_quantifier.benefit: No text can make the check last long enough to block the program.

signature_check_skipped_when_secret_unse.title: The signature of a webhook is only checked when a secret is set
signature_check_skipped_when_secret_unse.risk: A webhook (a call another service sends to your server) is checked only "if the secret is set". When the secret is empty or forgotten in the settings, every request is accepted, so anyone can send fake calls.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Refuse the request when the secret is missing (if not secret: raise …), then always check the signature.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

signature_check_skipped_when_secret_unse.benefit: A forgotten setting blocks the webhook instead of opening it to everyone.

sql_injection_format_string_python.title: A database query is built by inserting values with %
sql_injection_format_string_python.risk: The values are inserted into the text of the SQL query with % before it is sent to the database. If one of them comes from a user, that user can add their own SQL, for example to read or delete all data.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Pass the values separately and let the database driver insert them: cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = %s", (name,)), with a comma and not %.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

sql_injection_format_string_python.benefit: A value from a user can no longer change your queries.

sql_order_by_injection_python.title: The sort order of a query (ORDER BY) is taken from the request
sql_order_by_injection_python.risk: The column after ORDER BY is pasted from a value sent by the visitor, and this part of a query cannot be passed as a parameter. An attacker can add their own SQL there, for example to read data from other tables.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Accept only the column names you list: ALLOWED_SORT = {"name", "price"}, and take a default column when the value is not in the list.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

sql_order_by_injection_python.benefit: The visitor can only choose among your columns, not write SQL.

ssl_no_cert_validation.title: The certificate of the server is not checked (verify=False)
ssl_no_cert_validation.risk: With verify=False, the program accepts any server that answers, without checking its certificate (its proof of identity). Someone on the network can pose as the server and read or change the exchanged data, passwords included.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove verify=False; if the server uses a certificate of your own company, give its file instead: requests.get(url, verify="/etc/ssl/company-ca.pem").
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

ssl_no_cert_validation.benefit: Your program only talks to the real server, and the exchanged data stays private.

ssrf.title: The server fetches an address chosen by the visitor
ssrf.risk: An address from the request goes straight into requests, httpx, aiohttp or urlopen. An attacker makes your server call internal services that only it can reach, such as the cloud address 169.254.169.254 that hands out access keys.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Accept only the hosts you expect: parse the address with urlparse(url) and call it only if parsed.hostname is in your list of allowed hosts (ALLOWED_DOMAINS).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

ssrf.benefit: Your server only contacts the sites you chose.

ssrf_pdf_generation.title: A PDF or screenshot tool loads an address chosen by the visitor
ssrf_pdf_generation.risk: An address from the request is passed to pdfkit, imgkit, WeasyPrint or a browser driven by code, which loads it from your server. An attacker can point it at internal services and get their content back inside the PDF.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Check the address before converting it: 1) accept only https and the hosts on your list (urlparse(url).hostname in ALLOWED_HOSTS); 2) refuse names that lead to private addresses (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x, 127.x).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

ssrf_pdf_generation.benefit: The conversion tool only loads pages you allowed.

tarfile_unsafe_extract.title: A tar archive is extracted without checking where its files go
tarfile_unsafe_extract.risk: extractall() writes each file of a tar archive at the path written inside it. An archive sent by an attacker can contain paths such as ../../app/settings.py and overwrite files outside the target folder.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Extract with the built-in filter of Python 3.12 and later, tar.extractall(path=dest, filter="data"), or with an older Python check the path of each file before extracting it.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

tarfile_unsafe_extract.benefit: Files from an archive can only land in the folder you chose.

unbounded_allocation_from_declared_dimen.title: An image is created at the size a file claims, with no maximum
unbounded_allocation_from_declared_dimen.risk: The width and height used to create this image are read from the file itself, with no upper limit. A small crafted file can claim a huge size and make the program reserve gigabytes of memory, until it stops.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Check the width and height against a maximum before creating the image (for example width * height <= MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS), and reject the file otherwise.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unbounded_allocation_from_declared_dimen.benefit: A small file can no longer use up the memory of the program.

unbounded_parse_loop.title: A reading loop has no limit and can run forever
unbounded_parse_loop.risk: This while True loop reads data until it finds an end marker, with no limit on the number of turns. If a file or message never contains that marker, the loop never stops and blocks your program.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Give the loop a maximum (a number of turns or of bytes read) that does not depend on the end marker, write while consumed < MAX_BYTES: instead of while True:, and raise a clear error when the maximum is reached.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unbounded_parse_loop.benefit: A damaged or crafted file can no longer freeze your program.

unsafe_shell_construction.title: A shell command is built by joining text, with shell=True
unsafe_shell_construction.risk: The command is assembled with + or % and run by the shell (the program that reads command lines). If a value holds ; or $(...), the shell runs the extra command, with your program's rights.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Pass the command as a list, without shell=True: subprocess.run(["echo", name]), so that each value stays a single argument.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unsafe_shell_construction.benefit: No value can add a command of its own.

weak_password_hash.title: A password is hashed with a fast function (SHA or MD5)
weak_password_hash.risk: MD5 and SHA are fast: a graphics card tries billions of passwords per second against a stolen hash (a one-way fingerprint of the password). If your database leaks, most passwords are found within hours.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Hash passwords with a function made to be slow, such as bcrypt: bcrypt.hashpw(password.encode(), bcrypt.gensalt()), checked with bcrypt.checkpw().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

weak_password_hash.benefit: A stolen password database takes years, not hours, to crack.

weak_random_python.title: Weak random number generator
weak_random_python.risk: random module is not cryptographically secure; predictable values enable attacks.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use secrets module for security-sensitive operations: secrets.token_hex().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

weak_random_python.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security (CWE-330, OWASP A02).

zip_bomb.title: An archive is opened with no size limit
zip_bomb.risk: A ZIP archive is opened without checking the size of its content once unpacked. A small archive sent by an attacker can unpack to many gigabytes and fill the disk or memory of your server.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Add up the unpacked sizes before extracting, sum(f.file_size for f in zf.infolist()), and refuse the archive when the total exceeds a limit you choose (for example 100 MB).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

zip_bomb.benefit: A crafted archive can no longer fill your server.
